summary: Research the Godot-specific questions behind the Neon Static plan: web export limits, gameplay tech, viewfinder, testing, assets and licences, hosting, and the existing Umbara workflow

research.topic: How the existing Umbara Godot project is organised: process, tooling, tests, lessons, settings, reusable code, and the abandoned browser build
research.summary: Umbara (/Users/nimamovahedi/Projects/umbara) is a Godot 4.7 desktop FPS built by an AI-agent pipeline with a human who plays builds and picks between side-by-side pictures. The process is worth copying: a PLAN with the creator's decisions at the top, a STATUS board that says who owns which files, briefs with numbered pass checks, reports under 300 words, a single orchestrator who commits, and a hard two-Godot-instance limit enforced by tools/gslot.sh. The tooling that transfers is small and mostly generic: gslot.sh, check.sh, check_scripts.gd, the bot-run wrapper, the screenshot "shot" mode idea, the before/after pair-sheet script and the weapon-sandbox pattern. The test bot (godot/scripts/bot.gd, 1377 lines) is the most valuable idea but is welded to Umbara's level and objective code, so only the pattern carries over. The project's own audits, written after the fact, show what went wrong: a 2,324-line main.gd mixing ten jobs; the same objective logic written in four places; test and capture hooks inside gameplay code; hard-coded numbers outside cfg.gd; story text contradicting the fights; no fair-enemy rules (tells, pauses); no front end or save/continue. Levels 2 and 3 were not beatable by the average bot at baseline. Tool files are Mac-only (hard-coded /opt/homebrew/bin/godot, perl alarm, macOS paths). The project.godot is minimal (Forward Plus, MSAA 2x, 4096 shadows, no input map, default physics, no physics-engine setting). Its input uses raw Input.is_physical_key_pressed polling with a hand-kept key list, which caused a real bug (key 9 never read). Forward Plus is not available in a Godot web export, so the renderer settings and the Smart Graphics add-on must not be copied for Neon Static's later web build. The browser build mentioned in the notes was a different engine (Three.js/Vite), frozen when Nima moved to Godot for realism and effort reasons; it was not a Godot web export, so nothing here tells us anything about Godot web problems. I did not run any script or Godot, as instructed.

findings.point: One PLAN.md with a 'creator's decisions' table at section 0 that overrides everything else; audits and the draft plan sit below it.
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md tells every agent to read PLAN.md section 0 first, then its own brief, then STATUS.md, and 'nothing more than you need'. DESIGN.md (1,160 lines) is treated as searchable history, not reading material. Decisions are dated and recorded the same turn the creator makes them. The plan lists decisions as a table (release track, gun hold, length, scope, platform, order, check-in points). Copy this structure. Unflattering: the project's CLAUDE.md had to be rewritten on 2026-11-17 because it still described the old browser game, and DESIGN.md grew to 1,160 lines, so plain notes do rot.

findings.point: Planner/orchestrator writes briefs and is the ONLY one who commits; builders never commit, push, or edit outside their brief; testers only check against pass checks.
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md: 'Fable (orchestrating chat) plans, writes briefs with pass checks, reviews, and is the only one who commits. Opus build chats build exactly what their brief says, in the files their brief lists. Sonnet testers check work against the pass checks.' Builders must write docs/overhaul/reports/<brief id>.md under 300 words (files changed, check.sh output, where screenshots are, each pass check as PASS / FAIL / NOT CHECKED, things noticed outside the brief), then stop and not start follow-up work. Local git only, never push. Briefs also forbid git stash/checkout/reset. Review rule from PLAN: after three failed rounds the orchestrator stops and brings it to the creator. Earlier rule (LESSONS.md): sonnet agents sometimes returned wrong or unfinished reports, so read their diffs before trusting them. Git history shows about 56 commits, one per approved step.

findings.area: 1 Workflow: status board and file ownership
findings.point: STATUS.md is a table: ID, work, lane, state, 'files it owns'. Only the orchestrating chat edits it.
findings.detail: Lanes: code (one chat at a time because they share files), art (Blender, separate files), sound, look. Rows say 'waits for G3 (same files)'. Also holds a 'checkpoints for the creator' list (gun sheet, walker clips, music samples, Level 1 play-test, final play-through), review notes, baseline numbers, and a 'handed back, not yet reviewed or committed' list with a snapshot file of git blob ids (build/review/snap-1117.txt). Unflattering: parallel chats still collided. G2 swapped weapons.glb/props.glb while G1 was building its sheet; the G1 builder had to make a scratch copy of HEAD. W1 route A edited walker.gd and level_extras.gd outside its brief because nobody owned them; those edits sat uncommitted while W2 started, so W2's brief had to say 'do not rework route A'. The file-ownership list is a good idea but not enough on its own for binary assets like .glb.

findings.area: 1 Workflow: brief format and pass checks
findings.point: Briefs have fixed sections and numbered, mechanically checkable pass checks; the tester gets only the pass checks.
findings.detail: Format (G1, G3, M1, W2): title; Builder/Lane/Tester/Reviewer; 'Read first' list; 'Why' with the creator's own words quoted and dated; 'What to build' numbered; 'Out of bounds' (files and topics); 'Pass checks (the tester gets only these)'; 'Rules' (Godot slots, no commits, scratch dir build/<id>/); 'Report'. Pass checks name numbers and tools: 'FRAME area 22% or less for every gun'; M1: integrated loudness between -18 and -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP, no run of 3 samples at full scale, loop joins below a stated jump; W2: foot SLIDE at most 1 cm, CLIP at most 2 cm, one-frame speed change at most 0.25 m/s and heading 2 degrees, four crawlers cost at most 0.5 ms more per frame with GSLOT_SOLO=1. The brief also asks for evidence the reviewer can look at (spectrogram PNGs, contact sheets as JPG) and printed before/after numbers. Weak spot: some checks are 'show it with the bot or an input test and say how'; G1 pass check 2 came back PARTLY FAIL (pistol gloves below the frame); G1 report check 7 was 'PASS at sheet size; finger-level close-ups not taken', i.e. self-graded and loose.

findings.area: 1 Workflow: limits on parallel Godot instances
findings.point: Never more than two Godot copies at once, windows or headless; every run goes through tools/gslot.sh.
findings.detail: The rule exists because chained or parallel captures overlapped and hung, and a second copy halves the frame rate (LESSONS.md section 4). Blender does not count. GSLOT_SOLO=1 holds both slots for frame-rate measurements. W2 brief: 'expect to wait; an empty log is a time-out, run it again.' CLAUDE.md also notes macOS has no 'timeout' command, so gslot.sh is the time limit. Unflattering: the V1 stage 2 test 'waits for free Godot slots' in STATUS, so slot contention directly slowed the pipeline; the pre-slot rule 'one Godot at a time' was in the lessons file as early as 2026-11-15.

findings.point: The creator decides from side-by-side pictures at fixed checkpoints, not from descriptions.
findings.detail: LESSONS.md: 'He decides from pictures, not descriptions' (3-6 options side by side: looks A-D, HUD 1-4, four model styles, six explosion styles). 'Ask before a round, not after.' 'He plays, then reacts in one sentence per problem.' 'Never report a visual you have not seen in a screenshot of the running game.' Plan: three checkpoints plus any look or sound choice. Examples: music went through three rounds of samples (A-C, D-H, I-K) picked by ear; the gun hold went through a two-variant sheet. Unflattering: the music was iterated three times and the creator's first three samples were rejected ('feel like fun dancing music'), and the pick is still open in STATUS; the 11 WAV samples are 80 MB and had to be git-ignored.

findings.point: Two-slot lock runner with a time limit. Generic and reusable almost as is.
findings.detail: Invoked: sh tools/gslot.sh <max seconds> <command...>. It mkdir-creates $TMPDIR/umbara-gslots/slot1 or slot2 as locks, polls every 2 s, frees stale slots whose pid file points at a dead process, stores its pid, uses a trap to free the slot, and runs the command via 'perl -e alarm shift; exec @ARGV' as the kill timer. GSLOT_SOLO=1 takes both slots (polls every 3 s). To change: rename the lock dir ('umbara-gslots'); optionally put the slot count in a variable. Works for any command, not just Godot. Weaknesses: polling, not a queue (no fairness); the slot is shared by everything on the machine including other projects if the lock dir name is the same; if the caller is killed with SIGKILL the stale-slot cleanup relies on kill -0; a time-out looks like an empty log (W2 brief says 'an empty log is a time-out').

findings.point: One test command: script compile check plus short bot smoke run per level; must end with CHECK PASSED.
findings.detail: Invoked: sh tools/check.sh (all), 'scripts' (a few seconds, headless), 'smoke "1 2"' (named levels), SECS=240 for longer. Scripts mode runs godot --headless -s res://tools/check_scripts.gd (31 lines: loads every .gd and .gdshader in res://scripts and res://tools, prints 'CHECK FAIL <path>' and 'CHECK DONE n ok, m bad', exit 1 on bad) and also greps for 'SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error'. Smoke mode launches one bot per level (each via gslot.sh, 3 s apart, backgrounded then wait) with --audio-driver Dummy, then counts 'SCRIPT ERROR' lines and '^BOT ' lines; PASS needs 0 errors and more than 5 bot lines. Logs in build/check/. Needs changing: GODOT path (/opt/homebrew/bin/godot, overridable by GODOT env), level list, the bot argument grammar, the 'BOT ... death' grep. Honest limitation: the smoke test only proves the game runs without script errors for 150 game seconds; the V1 report ran it with 4 deaths on Level 1 and still PASS. It cannot judge difficulty, fun or look. A scripts-only mode that only loads scripts does not catch runtime errors in rarely used paths (e.g. L5 not in check.sh; a separate L5 run was done by hand in the W1 report).

findings.point: Wrappers and a report generator around the test bot; the report script is reusable if the summary.json schema is kept.
findings.detail: bot_runs.sh: sh tools/bot_runs.sh "level=1 diff=easy" "level=2 diff=medium enc=1" runs each option string one at a time (alarm 3000 s), filters output to BOT lines and SCRIPT ERROR, warns if other Godot processes exist (uses pgrep -ix godot; the process is named 'Godot' with a capital G). PROJECT= and OUT= environment overrides. Note it does NOT use gslot.sh, so it bypasses the two-copy rule. baseline.sh: runs every level on Medium in parallel pairs through gslot.sh with limit seconds and prints a per-level digest. bot_report.py (143 lines, needs Pillow): reads build/bot/<run>/summary.json and prints a markdown table per line (time, deaths, damage, kills, squad losses, scans, peak enemies, tanks, fps avg/worst) plus an intensity chart (enemies alive as a line, damage per 10 s as bars, phases shaded). To reuse: the table columns are Umbara-specific (scans, Y-wing strikes, tanks, squad); keep the intensity-chart idea (alive count and damage taken per 10 s against time) and the fps block (avg, worst ms, p95, p99).

findings.area: 2 Tool: screenshot capture (shot mode), visual_views.sh, visual_pairs.py, sheet.py
findings.point: Fixed named camera views captured by the game itself, then laid out as before/after pair sheets for the creator.
findings.detail: Game side: 'godot --path godot -- shot level=1 view=<s>,<lat>,<turn> weapon=<id> nohud out=<abs dir> snaps=15,25 vp=off' (main.gd _screenshot_mode, about 150 lines in main.gd:237-383; freezes and makes the player invulnerable; its snapshot timer does not run during the ride; view beyond the line limit is pulled back). tools/visual_views.sh <out> [only "names"] [extra args]: eight fixed views (ride, landing, forest floor, firefight, tank, gun, figures, sky) captured the same way every time, each through gslot.sh, greps for SCRIPT/SHADER/Parse errors. It also supports per-feature switches (vp=off, vp=-road,-shapes) so a change can be judged with each part off alone. tools/visual_pairs.py (Pillow): stacks before and after PNGs into labelled pair-*.jpg plus a small all-pairs.jpg overview. tools/sheet.py is a 2x2 style-sheet layout from the earlier browser/Blender style rounds, nearly unused now. shot.sh is the OLD browser build's headless-Chrome screenshot tool and is dead for Godot. Honest limits: captures are stills; V1 'Shimmer in motion: NOT CHECKED'; the muzzle-flash light turned tanks green in one frame in roughly one in seven captures and confused review (pair 5 had to be retaken); no two firefight captures match exactly because AI is not seeded.

findings.area: 2 Tool: build_app.sh, sandbox.sh, phase1_shots.sh, copy_skins.sh, synth scripts
findings.point: Smaller scripts: Mac app export, sandbox launcher, and Umbara-specific asset helpers.
findings.detail: build_app.sh (9 lines): cd godot, rm -rf ../build/Umbara.app, 'godot --headless --path . --export-release "macOS" ../build/Umbara.app'; needs the 4.7.2 macOS export template in ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates; about a minute. For the new project: change the app name and preset; add a Web preset and an output path (note it needs the web template, not installed). sandbox.sh opens a dev scene (weapon_sandbox.tscn) that shows every first-person gun side by side; pattern worth copying: one 'lab' scene per tricky subsystem that prints measured numbers (also walker_lab.tscn, tank_today.gd). phase1_shots.sh is an older one-off capture script; copy_skins.sh is for downloaded-model textures and not reusable. synth_music.py (2,376 lines) writes music as WAV/OGG using Blender's bundled numpy; synth_sounds.py (194 lines) synthesises 7 sound sets; user_sounds*.py reshape the creator's own recording. These are Umbara-specific in content (all notes original, but tuned to its brief) though the approach (Python synth run with 'python3 tools/synth_music.py', byte-identical reruns, layer loops by intensity, ffmpeg ebur128 checks) is reusable for a sound-from-code approach.

findings.point: A scripted 'average player' bot drives the real player through hooks; it found real problems but cannot judge feel.
findings.detail: godot/scripts/bot.gd (1,377 lines): launched with 'godot --path godot -- bot level=N diff=medium [enc=N] [limit=secs] [shots=0] [out=dir] [skill=average|sharp] [sound]'. It does not take the real mouse or keyboard; main.gd calls bot.drive(delta) after reading input (hook at main.gd ~1952), and player.gd exposes bot_move, bot_sprint, bot_jump. Skill profile 'average' (turn 3.2, initial aim error 0.11 rad settling over 1.6 s, 0.45 s reaction, only notices firing/scanned enemies within 55 m, bursts of 0.7 s, 22 s scan gap) was added because the first bot 'is playing with very high accuracy and speed, and is not representative'. It logs per line time, deaths, damage taken, kills, squad losses, frame stats (avg, worst, p95, p99) and a 10 s intensity trace, saves screenshots at key moments, mutes the master bus unless 'sound' is passed, and checks for other Godot processes. It includes unstick logic and a stall-watch. Results at baseline: L1 finished in 9.3 min with 1 death; L2 not finished (11 deaths at line 2, gave up at 18 min); L3 not finished (5 deaths at line 1 in 3 minutes); L4/L5 not finished. The bot did uncover soft locks and design problems (Level 3's second beacon unreachable for 23 minutes; escorts that never arrive; Y-wing strikes finishing objectives in 22 s). Honest limits stated in its header: it 'cannot judge fun, readability or how anything feels'. At baseline two games ran at once at about 38 fps, so timing numbers are rough. The audit that produced the time-to-kill tables was code-reading only ('Did not run the game'), so some timings were computed, not measured.

findings.area: 3 Testing approach: headless checks, labs, and evidence
findings.point: Layers: compile check, bot smoke, per-subsystem lab scenes with numeric pass checks, screenshots, and audio analysis with ffmpeg.
findings.detail: (1) check_scripts.gd headless compile of every script and shader. (2) 150 s bot smoke per level. (3) Labs: godot/tools/walker_lab.gd (978 lines), weapon_sandbox.gd (619 lines), tank_today.gd, hands_stage.gd, dump_grips.gd, inspect_gun.gd; they print FRAME, SLIDE, CLIP, 'feet within N cm of ground' lines so a brief's pass check can be a number. (4) Contact sheets and short clips (clips/W1, sheets/G1, V1). (5) Audio: spectrogram and loudness PNGs plus ffmpeg ebur128. (6) A checklist from the creator's game-dev skills (docs/SKILL_CHECKLIST.md): time-to-kill tables, fair-enemy rules (0.3-0.6 s reaction, first 1-2 shots miss), no AI state flicker, stuck checks, 1 - exp(-rate*dt) smoothing, audio on named buses, p95/p99 frame times. Honest weak spots: nothing runs in a real window at Retina size in the checks; 'Shimmer in motion: NOT CHECKED'; the smoke check lets deaths pass; Level 4 and 5 baselines never completed; the 'Smart Graphics' add-on re-applied saved settings and left wrong shared settings so V1 added a per-frame _hold_look() guard that forces mist, bloom and SSAO every frame, flagged as debt for P1.

findings.point: The audit's biggest finding is structural: a god-script, duplicated objective logic, and test hooks inside gameplay code.
findings.detail: main.gd is 2,324 lines mixing ten jobs (boot and capture harness, model building, combat services, squad, gunship, encounter director and phase machine, pickups and shop, abilities, settings/save, key polling and HUD text). 'Each objective type is implemented in four places' (main._update_objective, the HUD text branch in main._process, hud._objective_points, level_extras), which is why HUD wave counters disagree and why death/reset rules differ per type (B5, B6, B13). level_extras.gd is 'a grab-bag of five unrelated features driven by optional constants'. Test switches (Cfg.iso A/B variants), 150 lines of _screenshot_mode, perf logging and bot hooks sit inside the playing code. Dead code: RIDE_SHOOTDOWN (~65 lines), VENATOR_CRASH, withdraw state, DEFENCE.spider. Numbers hard-coded in code instead of cfg.gd (wave sizes, timers, spawn distances, AT-TE speed) despite the rule 'tuning numbers live in cfg.gd'. Stale headers/comments. Proposed fix (never done; T1 is still waiting): flow.gd state machine, one object per objective type with start/update/progress_text/markers/on_reset, dev_harness.gd, battlefield.gd, shop.gd, and input actions instead of a hand-kept WATCH key list. Recommendation for Neon Static: define one mission-type object interface and a separate dev harness from day one.

findings.area: 4 Lessons: flow bugs that map to Neon Static (death/retry, state reset, save)
findings.point: 17 flow bugs, most of them about what resets on death and about never wiring up save/continue.
findings.detail: B1 dying in the final fight replays the whole last line (69-81 enemies); B2 a timeout kills you and the explanatory banner is overwritten one line later; B5 finished objectives stay finished after a death so a line completes on its first frame; B6 the gate is never rebuilt after death; B7 'restart from checkpoint' gives Hard players checkpoints; B8 points and weapons lost between levels; B9 save.json written on every secure but never read, so no Continue; B10 pausing during a timed opening skips it; B4 shop item 9 can never be bought because KEY_9 is not in the hand-kept WATCH list; B17 every respawn drops free kit. R5: every level ends with the same placeholder end text; R13: an unskippable 21 s opening replays on every restart. Neon Static has no death but has failure/retry and money/reputation: design 'what resets' as one function owned by one state object, show why a failure happened, make intros skippable, and decide on save/continue in the first milestone.

findings.point: Enemy AI got stuck or acted unfairly because there were no stuck checks and no tell-before-fire rule; armour was unreadable.
findings.detail: H1 rushers inside 14 m fire about 5 shots a second with no aim state or glow because the rest timer is thrown away each frame; M6 Umbarans have no stuck check (only the friendly clones have a 2 s jam test) and can run in place against a tree forever; M7 hiders with no target kneel forever; M8 a guard tank shuttles across the road forever; M9 tanks have no stuck timer or collision with trees (they move by setting global_position); M10 AT-RT walks through trees; M12 per-frame clear_shot raycasts over all trunks make AI the main CPU cost; L10 smoothing used lerpf(..., 0.3) per frame (frame-rate dependent) in two places. Armour hits looked and sounded the same as flesh (M4). Bullets were nearly useless against armour (hover front 314 s of carbine fire) and one charged weapon dominated. For Neon Static (stealth plus pursuit): give every NPC a stuck timer and a state-change cooldown from day one; give detection and chase AI a visible tell; use exp(-k*dt) smoothing everywhere; keep perception staggered and raycasts cheap-first (SKILL_CHECKLIST says the same).

findings.point: Every level used the same template, there were no quiet stretches, and 'kill everything' conditions caused stalls; this made levels long and samey.
findings.detail: 25 'kill everything that comes down the road and both flanks' phases across 5 levels; per level about 300-430 enemies; fixed unskippable waits (21 s ride, 12 s intermissions, 22 s captures); two kill-all phases back to back at every level end. LESSONS: 'Nothing in Levels 1-3 has a quiet stretch'; the bot's intensity trace was flat-high from the first second; a counterattack can stall on stragglers (fix: after 20 s without a kill everyone left charges); strong tools short-circuit objectives (two Y-wing strikes finished Level 1's first objective in 22 s); the squad finished 'find it' objectives from 100+ m; objectives must be reachable from every side (a beacon 12 m off the road wedged the bot); decor you can walk into breaks the picture (tentacles with no collider filled the screen with magenta); story lines contradicted fights ('the gate is down, take the city' followed by 30 soldiers and 3 tanks). Rules adopted: draw the intensity curve first, 20-40 s recovery after each checkpoint, one new thing per encounter, finite waves tied to the objective, timers only where pressure is the point, difficulty scales accuracy/damage/aggression/numbers, never enemy health. Relevant to Neon Static's endless career: incident templates will repeat unless each incident type varies one new thing.

findings.area: 4 Lessons: assets, licences and cost of third-party models
findings.point: 16 of 35 models were downloaded with no author or licence on file, which blocked any release and forced a large rework.
findings.detail: ASSET_INVENTORY/PLAN: 35 models loaded, 19 in-house, 16 downloaded with no author or licence recorded (clone trooper, gunship, AT-RT, AT-TE, ships, five guns...). 15 of 29 sound sets were of unknown or franchise origin; 7 Kenney CC0 and 1 Pixabay were safe; 7 synthesised here. Every downloaded model was tracked in git and the app export shipped every file, used or not (export_filter all_resources). Godot would not load JPEGs embedded in downloaded glTF models, so skins had to be copied out (copy_skins.sh, model_skin.gd); downloaded models face +Z while the camera looks down -Z. The game stays private while CREDITS.md has blanks. The old browser build's rule was 'Confirm the licence of each pack before using it and record it in assets/LICENSES.md', apparently not followed for the later downloads. Recommendation: record author, URL, licence and date for every file at the moment it enters the repo.

findings.point: A list of engine and project gotchas to avoid repeating.
findings.detail: From LESSONS.md section 4: run 'godot --headless --path godot --import' once on a new checkout so class_names register (and after any model change); all copies of the project share one user:// folder (settings.json, save.json, add-on cfg) so test runs must not write saves; add-ons can change settings before your code runs (Smart Graphics defaulted to 8x MSAA a frame after start); the Godot process is named 'Godot' (pgrep -ix godot); a 'pgrep -f' wait loop matches its own shell and waits forever; ':=' cannot infer from untyped dictionary/Variant values; in Godot 4.7 a freed object compares equal to null so write 'if not is_instance_valid(x): x = null'; never reuse a level-data key for a different meaning (beacon hold vs relay hold); test runs silent with --audio-driver Dummy; shader warm-up by drawing every model and effect tiny for two frames (landing stall 148 ms to 13 ms); build fighters from a spawn queue at 3.5 ms a frame; forest cut into 40 m squares with LODs, drawn to 230 m, shadows to 70 m, trunk lookups through an 8 m grid; 'Retina: open the window in points, not pixels; draw the 3D world at no more than about 1.65 MP and upscale with FSR'. I did not verify these against Godot docs; they are the project's own recorded experience (anecdote from its own runs).

findings.point: The renderer is Forward Plus with MSAA 2x and a 4096 shadow map; there is NO input map, NO physics engine setting and NO custom layer names. Do not copy it blindly for web.
findings.detail: [application] config/features 4.7, 'Forward Plus'; run/main_scene res://main.tscn. [autoload] SmartGraphicsSettings (a third-party add-on). [display] window 1600x900, vsync_mode=1 (enabled). [rendering] renderer/rendering_method=forward_plus; textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true; anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d=2; directional_shadow/size=4096, soft_shadow_filter_quality=3; volumetric_fog volume_size=96, volume_depth=96. [editor] movie_writer mjpeg_quality=0.96. Nothing sets physics/3d/physics_engine, so the game uses Godot's default 3D physics; collision is mostly CharacterBody3D move_and_slide for the player and enemies are moved by setting global_position (so no real physics for NPCs). Input is read in code with Input.is_physical_key_pressed(KEY_...) and a hand-kept WATCH list in main.gd:136, not through the input map; rebinding is therefore impossible without rewriting. Forward Plus is desktop-only; Godot's web export cannot use it (needs 'Compatibility' / gl_compatibility). I did NOT verify this web restriction in this local task, so Neon Static's research on the web export should confirm it. For Neon Static: use the Mobile or Compatibility renderer plan early, define input actions in the input map, and test the web preset before the look is locked.

findings.point: A single macOS preset, universal, ad-hoc signed, private; excludes only dev scenes and shots.
findings.detail: export_presets.cfg [preset.0] name 'macOS', platform macOS, runnable=true, export_filter='all_resources' (everything ships including unused downloaded models), exclude_filter='shots/*, fx_preview.tscn, anim_preview.tscn, scripts/fx_preview.gd, scripts/anim_preview.gd', export_path ../build/Umbara.app, script_export_mode=2 (compressed binary tokens). Options: distribution_type=1, binary_format/architecture='universal', bundle_identifier 'local.umbara.game', version 0.6, copyright 'Private fan project, not for distribution', min_macos_version_arm64 11.00, display/high_res=true, codesign/codesign=1 (ad-hoc), no notarization, no entitlements. Not set: icon (empty), no Windows or Web preset exists. Weakness: 'Mac only, unsigned'; no key rebinding or controller. The dev scenes in godot/tools (labs, sandbox) are not in the exclude filter, so they ship in the app. P1 'export only used files' was never done. For Neon Static: use 'export_selected_scenes' or a tighter exclude_filter, and add the Web preset with the proper template.

findings.point: player.gd, check_scripts.gd, parts of gait.gd and the bot's skeleton are IP-free and reusable; combat, level and art files are not.
findings.detail: IP-free and reusable: (a) godot/scripts/player.gd (180 lines): CharacterBody3D first-person controller with acceleration/deceleration, sprint, jump, mouse look with look_scale tied to FOV, recoil as a spring that settles, head bob, strafe lean, landing dip as a damped spring, trauma-squared shake with summed sines, scope drift, bot_move/bot_sprint/bot_jump hooks for a test bot, 'frozen' and 'riding' flags. All smoothing uses 1 - exp(-k*dt). Constants: WALK 4.6, SPRINT 7.4, JUMP 4.8, GRAVITY 15, EYE 1.68, capsule 0.4 x 1.8 (radius 0.4, height 1.8), camera.far 9000. It captures the mouse on any mouse button press and releases on Esc. Contains an Umbara comment about the helmet lamp but no franchise content. Needs for Neon Static: crouch, camera zoom or viewfinder lean, no weapon/aim coupling ('aim', 'scoped' fields). (b) godot/tools/check_scripts.gd (31 lines) as is. (c) godot/scripts/gait.gd (669 lines): planted-feet IK for legged machines; not needed for a human stealth game but its 'all smoothing exp(-k*dt)', two-bone IK and ground-height-callable pattern may help for a character. It carries comments about AT-RT/AT-TE (franchise names), so it would need its comments rewritten before reuse. (d) godot/scripts/cfg.gd pattern: a Cfg class with const dictionaries, static funcs; content (weapon names, SQUAD names like 'Hardcase', 'Tup', 'Dogma', 'Sketch', 'Ringo', 'Oz', 'Boil' etc.) is franchise IP and must NOT be copied. (e) godot/scripts/bot.gd skeleton: setup(game, args) parsing 'key=value' args; drive(delta) called each frame after input; _press() with frame stamps; events and per-segment records; _frame_stats() fps block with p95/p99; stall/stuck watch; _snap() screenshots; _write_summary() to summary.json. About 1,000 of its 1,377 lines are Umbara-specific (cover, detonators, Y-wings, shop, capture, tank logic). (f) godot/scripts/music.gd (209 lines) and sfx.gd (176 lines): intensity-based calm/battle/climax track switching and synthesised sound play on named Music/Effects buses (pause_menu.gd:460-478 routes buses); not read in detail, so mark unverified. (g) grading.gd (111 lines), model_skin.gd (52 lines), and the color_correction add-on (a .tres gradient plus LICENSE): not read in detail.

findings.area: 6 Not safe to reuse (IP or fragile)
findings.point: Everything with franchise names, designs or downloaded assets must not be carried over; some tooling is tied to Umbara's data.
findings.detail: Do not carry over: models (clone trooper, gunship, AT-RT, AT-TE, ships, guns), sounds (15 of 29 from unknown or franchise origin, creator's own gun recording), the main-theme and soundtrack files, Level files (level1..5.gd), weapon and squad names, radio lines, DESIGN.md history, CREDITS.md rows, tools/blender build scripts that build franchise-style props (build_clone.py, build_gunship.py, build_umbaran.py, etc.; their helper common.py may be generic but I did not read it). The add-on addons/smart_graphics_settings (author 'Smart Graphics Team', version 0.1.2, LICENSE file present, I did not read the licence text) rewrites graphics settings after start and caused the V1 hold-look workaround; do not reuse for a game that must run on any recent laptop and later on the web without checking its licence and behaviour. addons/color_correction has a LICENSE and README but I did not read them.

findings.area: 7 Earlier browser build and why it was dropped
findings.point: The earlier build was Three.js + Vite, not Godot; it was frozen (not deleted) when Nima chose better realism, via Unreal and then Godot. No Godot web-export attempt is documented.
findings.detail: docs/overhaul/CLAUDE_old_browser_build.md says: Three.js + Vite plain JavaScript, target 60 fps in Chrome on integrated graphics, budget under about 300 draw calls and about 500k visible triangles (F3 overlay), at most about 4 dynamic lights, hitscan blasters, no physics engine, gray boxes until Milestone 5. DESIGN.md (around lines 645-665, 2026-11-14): 'Nima chose Unreal over staying in the browser or Godot ... for a significantly more realistic look and feel'; effort comparison 'browser 1x, Godot roughly 1.5-2x, Unreal roughly 3-5x with editor work Claude cannot do or verify'; revised the same day to 'try Godot first, not Unreal'. DESIGN.md line 1049: 'the Godot build already runs natively (Metal), not in a browser'. The browser build's frozen status is stated in CLAUDE.md ('src/, index.html and archive/ are the old browser build: frozen, never edit'). Known browser-build limits recorded: pointer lock could not be driven by the automated browser ('the Claude app's browser pane refused', so a free-look fallback was added); the test browser stopped drawing frames when not visible; no audio in the test browser. The earlier 'archive/' folder was an even earlier attempt. So there is nothing here on Godot web export problems; I did not read the full DESIGN.md (1,160 lines), only grep hits, so reasons beyond realism and effort may exist.

findings.area: Scale and cost of the project
findings.point: The project is large and heavy: the main script is huge, the repo is 372 MB of .git, and a whole overhaul was needed after about 56 commits.
findings.detail: Sizes measured with du/wc: .git 372 MB, godot/ 391 MB, build/ 622 MB (git-ignored). main.gd 2,324 lines, bot.gd 1,377, walker_lab.gd 978, cfg.gd only 108 lines (the tuning rule was followed unevenly). 56 commits total. The 'overhaul' started 2026-11-17 after the creator found the game too long and buggy; as of that date only G1, G2, M1, W1, V1 stage 1 were done, and tidy (T1), flow bugs (B1), combat rules (C1), Level 1 rebuild (L1) were all still waiting. In other words the process produced art/tooling quickly but had not yet fixed the core structural debt. The creator's input was also heavy: gun hold, music rounds, and walker clips all needed his pick.

recommendations: Copy the process, not the code: PLAN.md with a dated creator-decisions table at the top, STATUS.md with a 'files it owns' column, numbered briefs with pass checks and an 'out of bounds' list, 300-word reports, one committer. Add a rule the Umbara project lacked: any binary asset (.glb, .blend) shared between lanes needs an owner too.

Copy tools/gslot.sh (rename the lock dir) and check_scripts.gd as they are. Rewrite check.sh around Neon Static's own smoke run, and make it also fail on non-zero 'fail' events from the bot, not only script errors. Make bot_runs.sh go through gslot.sh (the Umbara one does not).

Build the dev harness as a separate autoload from day one (capture views, bot driver, frame-time log, command-line args 'key=value'), so gameplay scripts have no test branches. This avoids Umbara's 150-line _screenshot_mode inside main.gd.

Design a mission object interface before writing the first two incident types: start(), update() -> done, progress_text(), markers(), on_reset(), fail rules. Umbara wrote each objective in four places and paid for it in bugs.

Write a test bot early, but small: it should walk a stealth route and a pursuit route using the same hooks (bot_move etc. in the player script), log per-incident time, detection events, money delta and fps (avg, p95, p99), and write summary.json. Keep an 'average player' skill profile with reaction time and aim error so the bot is not unrealistically good.
Put all tuning numbers in one cfg file and enforce it in review (grep for numbers in AI/flow scripts). Umbara's rule existed but wave sizes, timers and spawn distances still ended up in code.

Give every NPC a stuck timer, a minimum time in each state, a visible tell before it acts, and staggered perception with cheap-first raycasts from the first version. Use exp(-k*dt) smoothing everywhere.
Use the Godot input map (actions) instead of polling physical keys, so rebinding and menu hints work and no key is silently unread.

Pick the renderer for web early: do a one-day 'web export of an empty first-person scene' test before the look is locked, since Umbara's Forward Plus settings, volumetric fog, 4096 shadow map and the Smart Graphics add-on are desktop assumptions. (Web restriction not verified here; the other research topics should confirm it.)

Record author, source URL, licence and date for every third-party asset at the moment it enters the repo (CREDITS.md with zero blanks as a pass check), and keep downloads out of git until used. Umbara had 16 models with no licence record.

Show the creator side-by-side stills for every look decision, with each look change behind its own switch (vp=off style) so a before/after pair is cheap to make. Keep the 'never report a visual you have not looked at' rule and add a rule that motion-dependent features (rain, neon flicker, viewfinder noise) need a short clip, since Umbara's stills-only checks never judged motion.

Do not carry over any Umbara content (names, models, sounds, level files, radio lines, weapon names, the Blender scripts that build franchise-style props, the SQUAD names in cfg.gd). The generic first-person controller (player.gd) can be reused, with its aim/scoped/weapon coupling removed and its Umbara comments rewritten.
risks: Process overhead: Umbara needed a planner chat, builder chats, tester chats and a creator checkpoint for each look or sound choice; for a solo creator with no coding experience this is a lot of coordination, and STATUS shows the overhaul still had its bug-fix and tidy lanes waiting while art/tooling lanes finished.

Structure debt is the main schedule risk: if Neon Static copies Umbara's habit of putting flow, input, capture hooks and level logic into one main script, the same bug classes (death-reset bugs, duplicated objective logic, unread save file) will recur.

The test bot is expensive: bot.gd is 1,377 lines tied to Umbara's mechanics. A stealth-and-pursuit bot (sight cones, following a car through streets) is a new piece of work, not a copy, and a bot cannot judge feel, readability or fun; the creator's play-tests remain the real check.

Mac-only tooling: scripts hard-code /opt/homebrew/bin/godot, rely on perl alarm and macOS paths, and the weapon sandbox launcher uses zsh; none of it is tested for a web build or other machines. Export preset is macOS-only; no Web preset has ever been created or tried in this project, so the web path is unproven here.

Rendering assumptions: Forward Plus, volumetric fog, MSAA 2x, 4096 shadow maps and a graphics-settings add-on that overrides settings after start are not safe defaults for 'any recent laptop' or the web; Umbara itself measured only about 38 fps with two copies running and relied on a custom performance pass (spawn queue, shader warm-up, LODs, FSR upscale).

Licence debt: Umbara's downloaded assets with no licence record meant a large replacement effort; Neon Static's plan to use ready-made packs and AI-generated models repeats the risk unless every file's licence is recorded when added.

Shared user:// folder: all copies of a Godot project with the same name share one save/settings folder, so parallel test runs and the real app can overwrite each other's settings; avoid by giving test runs a separate project name or a no-save flag (the bot already skips writing saves).

Limits of this research: I only read files; I did not run Godot or any script, I did not read all of DESIGN.md, music.gd, sfx.gd, grading.gd, model_skin.gd, the add-on licences or the Blender scripts in detail, and the audits were themselves code-reading exercises (the flow audit says 'did not run the game'). Treat the timing and bug numbers as the project's own claims.
open_questions: Does a Godot 4.7 web export work with the renderer, shaders and effects Neon Static wants (the Umbara project never tried one, and its settings assume Forward Plus)? That needs the official docs and engine issues, not this local read.
Is a bot-driven stealth and pursuit test feasible within the creator's budget, or should the first versions use scripted replays (fixed camera path, fixed seed) plus the creator's play-tests?
Which Umbara tool files are actually generic enough to copy into the new project without edits (common.py in tools/blender, music.gd, sfx.gd, grading.gd were not read in detail)?
What were the licence terms of addons/smart_graphics_settings and addons/color_correction (LICENSE files exist but were not read), and are they appropriate to keep in a public web game?

Why did the V1 performance debt (the forced mist/bloom/SSAO guard) arise; is the cause the add-on's shared settings file, as STATUS says, or a separate bug? (V1 reports this but the fix is deferred to P1.)

research.topic: What a Godot 4.7 project gains and loses on Web export, and how to build a desktop app first without painting into a corner
research.summary: Web export in 4.7 is still WebGL 2.0 through the Compatibility (gl_compatibility) renderer only. There is no WebGPU in mainline, and the 4.7 release article lists no web change. A single project can use Forward+ on the desktop app and Compatibility on web. The project setting rendering/renderer/rendering_method has a built-in .web override that already defaults to gl_compatibility, and a --rendering-method CLI flag exists. The cost is that the two renderers do not look the same. Compatibility lights in non-linear sRGB with RGBA8 colour and 24-bit depth and no reverse Z. It has no volumetric fog, SSR, SSIL, SDFGI, VoxelGI, TAA, FXAA, SMAA, depth of field, CompositorEffects or compute shaders. Glow works but is a different, reduced implementation. The 4.7 docs say simplified SSAO and decals work in Compatibility, but I could not confirm either against a release note or PR, and the 4.6 renderer table shows decals as unsupported. For a rainy neon night city, the unflattering part is that the Forward+ look (volumetric fog, SSR wet streets, SSIL, SDFGI, depth of field) cannot ship to the browser. If Neon Static is developed in Forward+ and exported later, the art would have to be redone. The safe plan is to develop and sign off in Compatibility from day one, and treat Forward+ as an optional desktop upgrade. Web mechanics are workable: the official nothreads release template is about 10 MB zipped (godot.wasm is 39.5 MB raw, about 6.9 MB with brotli q11), single-threaded export needs no special headers, and Jolt is built into web templates. The risks are single-threaded CPU and physics cost, audio quality in single-thread mode, Safari's documented WebGL 2.0 problems, no occlusion culling in default web templates, the wasm32 memory ceiling in the official templates, and no verified performance numbers. Installing the web template from the command line is just unzipping three or four files into ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable/ (the Mac currently has only macos.zip there). Headless export uses `godot --headless --path <proj> --export-release "<Web preset>" <dir>/index.html`.

findings.point: Web export is WebGL 2.0 / Compatibility only; Forward+ and Mobile do not run in browsers; no official WebGPU
findings.detail: 4.7 'Exporting for the Web' page: 'Godot 4 web exports target WebGL 2.0 only, via the Compatibility renderer. Forward+ and Mobile are unsupported. WebGPU is not yet supported.' The renderer comparison table lists Web as supported only for Compatibility. Coverage of 4.7 says its main web addition is wasm64 build support (the SCons flag), with no WebGPU, and one outlet had to correct an article that wrongly claimed WebGPU. A community fork (godotwebgpu, 4.6.2, started March 2026) exists but is not mainline. Godot's priorities page says WebGPU would let Forward+/Mobile projects export to web in future, with no date.

findings.point: One project can be Forward+ on desktop and Compatibility on web via rendering_method.web override and CLI flag
findings.detail: ProjectSettings in the 4.7-stable source: rendering/renderer/rendering_method defaults to "forward_plus"; rendering/renderer/rendering_method.web defaults to "gl_compatibility"; rendering/renderer/rendering_method.mobile defaults to "mobile". The setting 'can be overridden using the --rendering-method <method> command line argument' with values forward_plus, mobile, gl_compatibility. Feature-tag overrides work as setting.<tag> in project.godot. Note get_setting() ignores overrides; use get_setting_with_override(). The docs warn that switching to or from Compatibility 'usually requires manual changes to scenes, lighting, and environments'. Compatibility's own note: lighting is done on non-linear sRGB-encoded colour, 'inaccurate' but 'may look acceptable'. Use RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method() at runtime, because the engine can fall back (Forward+/Mobile fall back Vulkan to D3D12 to Compatibility on 4.4+, and rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3 can be unchecked).

findings.point: Compatibility has no VoxelGI, SDFGI, SSIL, SSR, volumetric fog; LightmapGI renders but baking is limited
findings.detail: 4.7 renderer table (Compatibility column): VoxelGI no, SDFGI no, SSIL no, SSR no, volumetric fog no; depth and height fog yes; ReflectionProbe yes but 2 per mesh (Mobile 8, Forward+ up to 256); LightmapGI 'rendering supported; baking needs RenderingDevice hardware'. Forum/doc-search result (anecdotal) says baked lightmaps do not need RenderingDevice to render, so bake on the Mac under Forward+ and run in Compatibility; I did not test lightmap data portability. PCSS soft shadows, light projector textures and contact shadows: no. Lights: 8 omni + 8 spot per mesh (project settings rendering/limits/opengl/max_lights_per_object default 8; max_renderable_lights; max_renderable_elements default 65536; docs suggest lowering these on web to cut shader compile time), max 8 directional lights. Automatic instancing is Forward+ only; MultiMesh works and is the recommended route for many identical objects.

findings.point: Glow, tonemap, adjustments, depth/height fog, SSAO (simplified), screen/depth texture: yes. DOF, CompositorEffects, FXAA/TAA/SMAA, debanding: no
findings.detail: Glow: Compatibility uses a different, simpler implementation; glow_levels, strength, mix, map, normalized have 'no effect'; glow_blend_mode is always Screen. Colour is RGBA8 (no HDR), so glow_hdr_threshold and intensity generally have to be tuned lower (forum anecdote: threshold below 1.0). SSAO: 4.7 Environment doc says supported in Forward+ and Compatibility, not Mobile; the effect page says a simplified SSAO exists 'since Godot 4.6' with only Radius and Intensity adjustable (PR #109447, merged 2025-11-01). Depth of field: the CameraAttributes doc says it is Forward+/Mobile only, not Compatibility. Auto-exposure is Forward+ only. CompositorEffects: no. Custom fullscreen-quad post effects and hint_screen_texture / hint_depth_texture shader access: yes. Tonemappers Linear/Reinhard/Filmic/ACES/AgX and Adjustments (brightness/contrast/saturation/LUT): no Compatibility caveat in docs. Debanding: no (gradients in dark rainy skies and fog may band). Normal/roughness buffer: no, so screen-space effects that need it must be faked.

findings.point: Only MSAA 3D (no alpha-to-coverage) and SSAA are available in Compatibility
findings.detail: 4.7 AA page: MSAA available everywhere, max 8x, docs advise 2x or 4x; SSAA via rendering/scaling_3d/scale above 1.0 (2.0 gives 4x SSAA, expensive). TAA and FSR2 are Forward+ only; FXAA and SMAA 1x are Forward+ and Mobile only; the screen-space roughness limiter is not in Compatibility. MSAA 2D is not supported. So thin neon tubes and wires will alias unless MSAA is on, and rain and signage shimmer cannot be fixed by TAA. The setting rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d defaults to 0 and is only read at startup.

findings.point: Decals are listed as supported in 4.7 Compatibility (8 per surface, 64 per view), but the 4.6 table says unsupported; occlusion culling is absent from default web templates
findings.detail: The 4.7-era renderer table shows Decals supported in Compatibility with 8 per surface and 64 per view, adjustable. A fetch of the 4.6 renderers table summarised decals as unsupported, and a 4.3 forum report and third-party Compatibility decal plugins suggest it was missing earlier; I could not find the PR, so treat decals as 'new in 4.7, verify on your own build' (confidence medium). Particles: GPUParticles3D works in Compatibility but trails, SDF collision and emit_particle() are not available; a community proposal recommends CPUParticles on web as a workaround for problems (anecdote). Occlusion culling: ProjectSettings note says 'Due to memory constraints, occlusion culling is not supported by default in Web export templates' and needs a custom template built with module_raycast_enabled=yes (the official web build config in platform/web/detect.py sets module_raycast_enabled to False). Mesh LOD and visibility ranges work and the docs recommend them over occlusion culling for open scenes. SubViewport works in all renderers (documented in general, no Compatibility caveat found; I did not test).

findings.point: Directional (PSSM 4 split), omni (cube or dual paraboloid), spot shadows work; shadows are the big cost; PCSS soft shadows are not available
findings.detail: 4.7 lighting doc: positional shadow atlas default 4096 (2048 suggested for low-end), 88 shadowed lights in view with default allocation; omni shadow mode Cube (default, accurate) or Dual Paraboloid (faster, deformation); directional PSSM has 4 splits, and an object spanning all splits is drawn 5 times. In the renderer table, Compatibility renders shadowed lights multi-pass with 'less accurate blending'. Neon city implication: dozens of shadow-casting neon lights are not affordable; keep most neon as unshadowed omni/spot or emissive meshes plus glow.

findings.point: Single-threaded web export is the default and needs no cross-origin isolation; threaded needs COOP/COEP
findings.detail: Since 4.3 single-threaded is the default (export option variant/thread_support defaults to false in the 4.7-stable export plugin; variant/extensions_support also false). Threads and GDExtension need Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp, or the PWA service-worker workaround (progressive_web_app/enabled plus ensure_cross_origin_isolation_headers, default true). A secure context (HTTPS or localhost) is still required. The 4.3 progress report (2024-05-15, old) said single-threaded fixed long-standing playback issues on Apple devices and that in single-threaded builds audio rendering is tied to frame rate so frame drops garble audio. The 4.7 docs say the single-threaded export is less performant than threaded and WebAssembly is slower than native; no benchmark numbers are given in any official source I found.

findings.point: Measured 4.7.2 web template: godot.wasm 39.5 MB raw, about 10.2 MB deflate, about 6.9 MB brotli q11; official templates are wasm32 only
findings.detail: I read the official 4.7.2 export-templates .tpz (1,281,349,702 bytes) central directory and inflated two web templates. web_nothreads_release.zip (10,245,903 bytes) contains godot.wasm 39,514,754 bytes (10,168,063 deflated; gzip -9 10,054,758; brotli q11 6,902,599; brotli q9 7,889,576), godot.js 279,815, plus audio worklets, godot.html, service worker. web_release.zip (threads) godot.wasm is 38,820,072. Template files: web_[dlink_][nothreads_](debug|release).zip, so GDExtension builds (dlink) are about 1.5 MB larger zipped. The exported .pck holds all game assets and is the real size driver. The 4.3 article (2024) said wasm was about 40 MB raw and about 5 MB with brotli at that time. Official guidance: precompressed Brotli for .wasm and .pck, serve .wasm as application/wasm; wasm compresses to about a quarter with gzip; compile a custom template with unused modules disabled to shrink further. Export options for textures: vram_texture_compression/for_desktop (default true, S3TC) and for_mobile (default false); enabling both makes a larger but more compatible export, and Apple Silicon Safari/Chrome use S3TC/BPTC on desktop.

findings.point: No built-in streaming; PCK patches/DLC via load_resource_pack exist but the docs give no web guidance; memory is wasm32 in official templates
findings.detail: The 'Exporting packs, patches, and mods' page documents Export as Patch with Base Packs and ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack(); it says nothing about web, so splitting a web build into several .pck files fetched at runtime is not an documented, supported path (you would need to fetch bytes with HTTPRequest, write to user://, then load the pack; unverified). Memory: in platform/web/detect.py, initial_memory defaults to 32 MiB with ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1; wasm64 (MEMORY64) is a build-time arch option added by SCons PR GH-102378 in 4.7, but the official export plugin only advertises the wasm32 feature tag and the official tpz contains no wasm64 templates, so a 4 GB-class ceiling remains in practice unless you compile custom templates. The docs state no memory limit figure. Browsers also can block big allocations, so keep texture memory small; Safari reloaded the Platformer 2D demo with a 'significant memory' warning (2024 anecdote from the same article).

findings.point: Web default is Sample playback mode (low latency, no effects); Stream mode adds latency especially without threads
findings.detail: Since 4.3, audio/general/default_playback_type has a .web override defaulting to 1 (Sample); other platforms 0 (Stream). Sample mode uses the Web Audio API and 'does not support AudioEffects, reverb/doppler, or procedural audio'; positional audio can be inconsistent. Set Default Playback Type.web to Stream or per-player Playback Type to Stream to use Godot's mixer, at the cost of latency and possible garbling when frames drop. Only static WAV/OGG/MP3 can be registered as samples. Web supports up to 5.1 channels. Browsers block autoplay until the first click/tap/key, so a start screen is mandatory. Relevance: a police scanner with radio filter/reverb effects and camcorder tape hiss want bus effects, which Sample mode cannot do; either design effects into the audio files or accept Stream mode on web.

findings.point: Pointer lock and fullscreen only work inside a user-input callback; Escape releases the lock
findings.detail: Official page: browsers only allow cursor capture and fullscreen from a user input event; call from _input/_unhandled_input; the fullscreen project setting only works if the engine starts inside a valid input handler, which needs a customised HTML page. The docs do not name an Escape behaviour; it is a standard browser behaviour (pointer lock is released with Esc, not Godot-specific, and games must show a 'click to resume' screen) - this part is my general knowledge, not from the Godot docs. A first-person game therefore needs a click-to-start/click-to-recapture overlay.

findings.point: user:// saves go to IndexedDB and can silently fail; C# cannot export to web; GDExtension needs special template and COOP/COEP
findings.detail: user:// persistence depends on IndexedDB: users must allow cookies, third-party cookies must be allowed in iframes, private/incognito prevents persistence, and OS.is_userfs_persistent() can return false positives. C#: the 4.7-stable export plugin refuses with 'Exporting to Web is currently not supported in Godot 4 when using C#/.NET'. GDExtension needs the Extensions Support option (variant/extensions_support, dlink templates), extensions compiled for web, and cross-origin isolation. Since the plan is GDScript-only, only the first applies. Also: tab is paused when not visible (_process stops), only HTTP/WebSocket/WebRTC networking exists, gamepads appear only after a button press.

findings.point: Official docs advise Chromium or Firefox over Safari because of WebGL 2.0 issues; no official native-vs-web numbers exist
findings.detail: 4.7 web page: 'Safari has several issues with WebGL 2.0 support that other browsers don't have' and recommends Chromium or Firefox. Anecdotes (forum/itch, 2022-2025, labelled anecdote): WebKit bug 247860 (Safari 16.1 crash on load, 2022), WebGL context loss on iOS and Safari after long play (4.3-era forum thread), SharedArrayBuffer freezes on macOS in old threaded builds. I found no Firefox-on-macOS specific official problem list and could not verify any. Performance: docs only say WebAssembly is slower than native and single-threaded is slower than threaded, and the renderer table calls Compatibility 'low base, high scaling' cost. There is no published figure, so plan to measure your own build on Safari, Chrome, and Firefox on the M4. On the same M4 the browser build should not be GPU bound, but CPU-side work (physics, GDScript, draw-call submission, shader compiles) runs in single-threaded wasm.

findings.point: Jolt is compiled into web templates and the module is built on every platform; but run_on_separate_thread is forced off in nothreads builds
findings.detail: 4.7-stable modules/jolt_physics/config.py: can_build returns not env['disable_physics_3d'] with no platform exclusion; SCsub has a web-specific branch (enables SSE4.2 for WebAssembly SIMD when wasm_simd, default True in detect.py), and compiles both JobSystemSingleThreaded and JobSystemThreadPool. register_types.cpp: run_on_separate_thread is read only when THREADS_ENABLED, else false. So in the default single-threaded web build Jolt runs on the main thread. This is source reading, not a runtime test; I found no official statement or benchmark. Caveat: physics/3d/physics_engine in 4.7 has DEFAULT equal to GodotPhysics3D; only projects created in 4.6+ explicitly store Jolt, so set 'Jolt Physics' explicitly. The docs call the 'Run On Separate Thread' setting experimental and not thoroughly tested; keep it off. Jolt's temporary_memory_buffer_size defaults to 32 MiB, which matters on web memory.

findings.point: Official templates are one 1.28 GB .tpz; macOS Mac currently has only macos.zip; install by unzipping into the version folder
findings.detail: Docs only describe the editor path (Editor > Manage Export Templates > Install from file). Command line: the 4.7.2 tpz is at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/download/4.7.2-stable/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_export_templates.tpz (1,281,349,702 bytes, published 2026-08-18; 4.7.1 on 2026-07-14, 4.7 on 2026-06-18). It is a zip whose members are under templates/ (verified from its central directory): web_release.zip, web_debug.zip, web_nothreads_release.zip, web_nothreads_debug.zip, web_dlink_*, plus templates/version.txt (13 bytes). On this Mac ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/ currently contains the folder 4.7.2.stable with only macos.zip and version.txt, as observed read-only. Command shape (not run): download the tpz to a scratch folder, then `unzip -j <tpz> 'templates/web_nothreads_*.zip' 'templates/web_release.zip' 'templates/web_debug.zip' -d "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable/"`. The folder name and version.txt come from the engine version string (4.7.2.stable); the macOS path convention is from my own knowledge and the existing folder, not from the docs. A smaller option is HTTP range requests for individual zip members, which I used to inspect two templates; not needed for normal use. Only the nothreads release template is needed for the planned build.

findings.point: Headless export uses --headless with --export-release <preset> <path>; the web preset must exist in export_presets.cfg
findings.detail: CLI docs: `--export-release <preset> <path>` and `--export-debug`, 'The preset name must match one defined in export_presets.cfg', path relative to the project dir, must include the file name, and 'the target directory must already exist'; `--export-pack` for pck only; `--headless` is 'equivalent to --display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy' and avoids opening a window on machines with a GPU. The web export file must end in .html (the plugin's binary extension). Example (not run): `Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --path <project> --export-release "Web" build/web/index.html`. Run `--import` first on a fresh checkout (--export-debug and --export-pack imply --import per docs; for release exports I could not confirm and it is safest to import first). Local test: the Godot repo's serve.py ('not for production'), or any static server with correct MIME types and, for threaded builds, the COOP/COEP headers. Web export preset must be created once in the editor, since export_presets.cfg does not exist yet.

findings.point: The Compatibility look differs from Forward+: sRGB lighting, RGBA8 buffers, no HDR, no debanding
findings.detail: Renderer table: Compatibility colour precision RGBA8 (low dynamic range), depth 24-bit with no reverse Z, no debanding, and the ProjectSettings text says lighting is done on 'nonlinear sRGB-encoded color data'. Forum/itch threads (anecdote, 2023-2025) repeatedly report web exports looking different or darker than the editor, including fog and glow differences. For a neon-on-black scene this hits the exact effects the game relies on (bloom, fog, wet reflections), so all colour and glow tuning should be done in the renderer that ships to the web.

recommendations: Develop and approve every milestone in the Compatibility renderer, even for the desktop app. Set rendering_method to gl_compatibility for the whole project and do not set a Forward+ default. Then desktop and web look the same, and the web port is mostly a packaging task.

If you want a prettier desktop-only mode later, treat it as an optional second tier: keep Forward+ out of the main scenes and add it only via rendering_method=forward_plus at the CLI or a feature-tag override. Tune a separate WorldEnvironment resource for it, selected with RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method(). Do not build gameplay or readability on it.

Fake the rainy neon night: no volumetric fog, no SSR, no SSIL, no SDFGI/VoxelGI, no depth of field. Use depth and height fog tinted by district, a bright emissive-plus-glow pass tuned for RGBA8 (glow_hdr_threshold probably below 1.0), emissive signs with unshadowed omni/spot lights, baked LightmapGI for static streets, ReflectionProbes (only 2 per mesh), a custom 'wet street' spatial shader with fake sky/neon reflection and a cubemap or planar SubViewport for a few hero puddles, rain as particle streaks plus a screen-space overlay, and decal-like puddle sheets as quads or 4.7 Decals after verifying them.

Make the old-camcorder viewfinder a single fullscreen post-process (a ColorRect or quad using hint_screen_texture) plus a SubViewport if needed, rather than depending on CompositorEffects. Do the blur/focus effect there (cheap downsampled blur in the shader) to fake depth of field, and add scanlines, chroma bleed, noise, tape wobble and vignette in the same shader. This works identically in Compatibility on web.

Lock these settings from day one: rendering/renderer/rendering_method=gl_compatibility; physics/3d/physics_engine=Jolt Physics set explicitly; physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread=false; rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d=2x (test 4x); rendering/limits/opengl/max_lights_per_object lowered (try 4), max_renderable_lights and max_renderable_elements lowered to measured needs; rendering/lights_and_shadows/positional_shadow/atlas_size 2048; a hard budget on shadowed lights (for example 1 sun/moon directional plus 2 to 4 shadowed spot/omni near the player, cars headlights only when needed); rendering/scaling_3d with a user-facing render-scale option; no occlusion culling (not in default web templates), use mesh LOD and visibility_range instead; audio/general/default_playback_type.web decision (Sample vs Stream) made early.

Design audio for web: pre-bake radio filtering, scanner squelch, static and camcorder hiss into the audio assets so that Sample playback mode (no bus effects) is acceptable, and keep a Stream-mode fallback for the few effect-heavy sounds. Add a click-to-start screen (autoplay, pointer lock, fullscreen all require a user gesture) and a click-to-resume overlay for pointer-lock loss, and put them in the desktop app too so the code path is shared.

Treat the first web export as a spike, not a late task: install the web template now (unzip web_nothreads_*.zip, web_release.zip, web_debug.zip from the 4.7.2 tpz into ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable/), create a Web preset with variant/thread_support=false and variant/extensions_support=false, and export an empty Compatibility scene with fog, glow, a few lights and a car-sized Jolt body. Test in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on the M4 and record frame time before adding any real content. Repeat after each milestone with a headless export script.

Keep the .pck small from the start: texture budgets (small atlases, 512 to 1024 px tiles, VRAM compression for desktop), low-poly models, OGG for music and WAV only for short effects, no unused fonts, export filters that exclude source art. Plan on brotli precompression for .wasm and .pck on the host and confirm the host (Cloudflare Pages/GitHub Pages/itch) serves .wasm as application/wasm. Do not plan on multi-pack streaming unless the first measurements force it.

Choose single-threaded export for the public site; do not depend on threads, GDExtension or C#. Keep CPU work off the web hot path: limit active AI cars, pedestrians and physics bodies, use MultiMesh for repeated props, prefer visibility ranges and simple collision shapes, and make GPUParticles3D effects short and capped or use CPUParticles3D for tiny effects.

Write the game with a thin 'platform' layer (settings, quality tiers, save/load, input capture) so web differences (user:// IndexedDB persistence that may fail, pointer lock, fullscreen, pause when tab hidden) are isolated. Save with a clear 'saving unavailable' warning if OS.is_userfs_persistent() is false, and offer an export/import-code or download fallback.
risks: The look you want (volumetric fog, SSR wet streets, SSIL, depth of field) is only possible in Forward+, which can never ship to the browser. Starting in Forward+ and 'toning down later' means re-lighting and re-tuning every scene, and the AI agent cannot judge the look; the creator would be the only look-judge.

Compatibility lights in sRGB with RGBA8 buffers and no debanding. Dark gradients (night sky, fog, light cones) can band, bloom behaves differently, and the web build can look darker than the editor view; there are repeated anecdotal reports of web lighting mismatches.

Single-threaded web build plus Jolt on the main thread, GDScript and many shadowed lights could miss frame rate in a driving-while-filming scene with traffic. No official benchmark exists; performance on Safari in particular is unmeasured here.
Audio on web: Sample mode forbids bus effects, and Stream mode in single-thread builds can garble when frames drop. The scanner and camcorder audio design may need baked effects.

Safari is officially described as having several WebGL 2.0 problems; Safari is the default browser on the creator's Mac and many players' laptops, and context loss anecdotes exist. Firefox on macOS was not verified at all.

Default web templates lack occlusion culling and are wasm32 only; the official templates give no 4 GB+ memory path, and a custom template (wasm64, raycast) means building the engine from source, which is a heavy task for a no-code creator.

Several claims here come from docs, source and release metadata that I read but did not run: Compatibility decals (docs table versus an older table), simplified SSAO quality, baked-lightmap portability from Forward+ to Compatibility, Jolt behaviour in a web build, and the headless export command. Nothing was executed except template inspection.

Download size: about 7 to 10 MB for the engine plus the pck; a rich city could push first-load time and memory use up fast, and the docs offer no official guidance for splitting or streaming a web pck.

verification.topic: Verification: Godot 4.7 Web export gains and losses, and how to build a desktop Mac app first that can still export to the web

verdicts.point: Web export is WebGL 2.0 through the Compatibility renderer only. Forward+ and Mobile do not run in browsers, and there is no WebGPU.
verdicts.correction: The 4.7 page says Godot 4 'can only target WebGL 2.0 (using the Compatibility rendering method)' and 'currently does not support WebGPU, which is a prerequisite for allowing Forward+/Mobile to run on the web platform.' I did not check the claims about the community fork or about media corrections.

verdicts.point: rendering/renderer/rendering_method defaults to forward_plus, the .web override defaults to gl_compatibility, the .mobile override defaults to mobile, the --rendering-method CLI flag exists, Compatibility lights in nonlinear sRGB, and get_current_rendering_method should be used at runtime
verdicts.correction: Confirmed word for word in the 4.7-stable ProjectSettings.xml (lines 3279-3292). One small fix to the fallback description: on macOS the Forward+ fallback is Metal, not Vulkan or D3D12. rendering/rendering_device/fallback_to_opengl3 (default true) 'will fall back to OpenGL 3 if Direct3D 12, Metal, and Vulkan are not supported'.

verdicts.point: Compatibility has no VoxelGI, SDFGI, SSIL, SSR or volumetric fog. LightmapGI renders, but baking needs RenderingDevice. 2 reflection probes per mesh. 8 lights per mesh. RGBA8 colour, 24-bit depth without reverse Z, no debanding. No DOF, compute or CompositorEffects.
verdicts.correction: The 4.7-stable renderer table and the Environment.xml notes match. Additional defaults from ProjectSettings: rendering/limits/opengl/max_renderable_lights is 32 and max_renderable_elements is 65536. These limits and max_lights_per_object apply only to Compatibility. The table I fetched does not list automatic instancing, auto-exposure or GPU-particle rows, so I could not confirm those claims from the table.

verdicts.point: Decals are supported in 4.7 Compatibility (8 per surface, 64 per view)
verdicts.correction: In 4.7 stable, decals are NOT supported in Compatibility. The 4.7 renderer table says 'Not supported', and 4.7-stable Decal.xml says 'Decals are only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.' The 'supported, 8 per surface, 64 per view' text comes from the docs/en/latest page, which tracks the master branch. That page warns it may describe features not in released stable versions, so this is an unreleased feature (likely 4.8+). Plan puddles and grime as textured quads or shader tricks. Do not plan on Decal nodes for the web build.

verdicts.point: SSAO works in Compatibility. Glow is a different, reduced implementation (glow_levels, strength, mix, map and normalized have no effect, blend mode is always Screen).
verdicts.correction: 4.7-stable Environment.xml: 'SSAO is only supported in the Forward+ and Compatibility rendering methods, not Mobile.' The glow notes match: levels/*, normalized, strength, blend_mode, mix, map and map_strength are unavailable or hidden. I did not verify the 'since 4.6, PR #109447' detail. The claim that glow_hdr_threshold needs to go below 1.0 is a forum anecdote.

verdicts.point: Anti-aliasing in Compatibility: MSAA 3D and SSAA only. TAA and FSR2 are Forward+ only. FXAA, SMAA and the roughness limiter are Forward+ and Mobile. msaa_3d defaults to 0 and is read only at startup.
verdicts.correction: The 4.7 AA page and ProjectSettings agree. Max MSAA is 8x, and the docs advise 2x or 4x. At runtime, use Viewport.msaa_3d to change it. I could not confirm the alpha-to-coverage claim from the page.

verdicts.point: Occlusion culling is not in the default web templates and needs module_raycast_enabled=yes
verdicts.correction: ProjectSettings note confirmed. detect.py sets module_raycast_enabled False with the comment 'Embree is heavy and requires too much memory (GH-70621)'.

verdicts.point: The positional shadow atlas defaults to 4096, with 2048 suggested for low-end hardware
verdicts.correction: The default is 4096. There is an automatic atlas_size.mobile override of 2048, but NO .web override. A web build keeps 4096 unless you set it yourself. I did not re-check the '88 shadowed lights' and 'drawn 5 times' figures.

verdicts.point: Single-threaded export is the default (variant/thread_support false, extensions_support false). Threads need COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp. The PWA option ensure_cross_origin_isolation_headers defaults to true.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed in the 4.7-stable export_plugin.cpp (lines 374-386) and on the 4.7 web page. progressive_web_app/enabled defaults to false.

verdicts.point: Template sizes: web_nothreads_release.zip is 10,245,903 bytes inside the 1,281,349,702-byte 4.7.2 tpz. Official templates are wasm32.
verdicts.correction: I read the tpz central directory myself with an HTTP range request. Uncompressed sizes: web_nothreads_release.zip 10,245,903, web_release.zip 10,290,815, web_nothreads_debug.zip 10,232,720, web_debug.zip 10,342,534. dlink variants are about 11.5-12.1 MB. macos.zip is 123,597,580. version.txt is 13 bytes. The export plugin pushes only the 'wasm32' feature. I did not re-measure the godot.wasm raw size or the brotli/gzip figures. The docs only say wasm compresses to 'around a quarter' with gzip.

verdicts.point: Memory: initial_memory is 32 MiB with ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH, and wasm32 gives a '4 GB-class ceiling' in practice
verdicts.correction: initial_memory 32 MiB and -sALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 are confirmed in detect.py, and wasm64 is a valid arch in 4.7-stable. However, detect.py does not set MAXIMUM_MEMORY, and Emscripten's documented default MAXIMUM_MEMORY is 2147483648 bytes (2 GB). The practical heap ceiling for official templates is therefore most likely 2 GB, not 4 GB. This is an inference from the build flags plus the Emscripten docs. I did not test it at runtime. The default stack size is 5120 KiB.

verdicts.point: The web default is Sample playback (audio/general/default_playback_type.web = 1), with no AudioEffects. Stream mode enables the full feature set.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed in 4.7-stable ProjectSettings and on the 4.7 web page. I did not re-check the 5.1-channel claim.

verdicts.point: Pointer lock and fullscreen only work from an input event. Escape releasing the lock is general browser behaviour, not something the Godot docs say.
verdicts.correction: The 4.7 page covers the input-event requirement and does not mention Escape. The report labels the Escape part correctly.

verdicts.point: C# cannot export to web, and GDExtension needs extension support plus web-compiled extensions
verdicts.correction: The exact error string is confirmed at export_plugin.cpp line 427.

verdicts.point: Safari has documented WebGL 2.0 issues, and the docs recommend Chromium or Firefox. There are no official native-vs-web performance numbers.
verdicts.correction: The quote is confirmed. The specific Safari bug and crash reports are anecdotes I did not re-check.

verdicts.point: Jolt is built for web (can_build has no platform exclusion, the web SIMD branch adds -msse4.2), run_on_separate_thread is forced false without THREADS_ENABLED, and physics_engine DEFAULT means GodotPhysics3D
verdicts.correction: Confirmed in config.py, SCsub and register_types.cpp, and in ProjectSettings ('DEFAULT is currently equivalent to GodotPhysics3D'; 'Jolt Physics is the default for projects created starting in Godot 4.6'). temporary_memory_buffer_size defaults to 32 MiB. Minor: the 4.7 ProjectSettings text for physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread does not call it experimental. That wording, if it exists, is somewhere else.

verdicts.point: Installing the web template means unzipping templates/web_*.zip from the tpz into ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable/, and this Mac currently has only macos.zip and version.txt there
verdicts.correction: Folder contents were observed read-only: 4.7.2.stable/ holds macos.zip and version.txt. The member names under templates/ are confirmed. The tpz was published 2026-08-18, 4.7.1 on 2026-07-14 and 4.7 on 2026-06-18 (GitHub API). The CLI unzip approach is not documented officially. The docs only describe the editor's Manage Export Templates install-from-file.

verdicts.point: Headless export: --headless --export-release <preset> <path>. The target directory must exist. --export-debug and --export-pack imply --import, and release export is not stated to.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed on the 4.7 CLI page. --headless is described as '--display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy'. The 'avoids opening a window on machines with a GPU' wording was not on the page. Running --import before a release export on a fresh checkout remains the safe advice.

verdicts.point: The 4.7 release article lists no web change, and 4.7's web addition is wasm64 build support
verdicts.correction: I did not open the 4.7 release article, so 'lists no web change' is unverifiable here. wasm64 as a supported arch (MEMORY64 flag) is confirmed in 4.7-stable detect.py. The PR number GH-102378 was not checked.

important_facts_missed: The report mixed docs/en/latest (master branch, unreleased) with docs/en/4.7 (stable). For anything that ships, use the /en/4.7/ docs or the 4.7-stable source tag. Decals are a concrete case: master says supported, 4.7 stable says not supported.

Decal nodes do not render in Compatibility in 4.7.x, so they do not render on web. Wet-street puddles, graffiti and blood spatter (the user chose 'some blood') must be textured quads, mesh-baked details or shader masks, not Decal nodes.

The Emscripten default MAXIMUM_MEMORY is 2 GB, and Godot's detect.py does not override it. The realistic memory ceiling for official web templates is likely 2 GB, not 4 GB (inference, not runtime-tested).
The shadow atlas has a .mobile override (2048) but no .web override. A web build keeps 4096 unless the project sets it.
rendering/limits/opengl/max_renderable_lights defaults to 32. Lights beyond that are silently ignored, which matters for a neon city with many omni lights.
On macOS the Forward+ fallback chain is Metal, then OpenGL 3 (fallback_to_opengl3 default true). D3D12 is Windows only.

Developing in Compatibility from day one also means the desktop Mac app runs on OpenGL 3.3, which Apple has deprecated (its OpenGL runs on top of Metal). That is fine on the M4 but worth a desktop smoke test. This is general knowledge, not from the Godot docs.
The tpz central directory also confirms the dlink (GDExtension) templates are about 11.5-12.1 MB, and macos.zip is about 123.6 MB uncompressed. The tpz holds 35 entries in total.
verification.corrected_bottom_line: The report holds up on almost every load-bearing point. Checked against 4.7-stable source and the /en/4.7/ docs, the following are all confirmed: web is WebGL 2 through Compatibility only, with no WebGPU. The rendering_method.web override defaults to gl_compatibility and the --rendering-method flag exists. Compatibility lacks volumetric fog, SSR, SSIL, SDFGI, VoxelGI, DOF, TAA/FXAA/SMAA, compute and CompositorEffects. It does have SSAO, a reduced glow, MSAA and SSAA. Single-threaded export is the default and needs no special headers. Sample audio is the web default. C# is blocked. Jolt is built for web but runs on the main thread. The template sizes are exact: web_nothreads_release.zip is 10,245,903 bytes. The template folder layout and the headless export flags are correct.
