There is one real error: decals are NOT supported in Compatibility in 4.7.x. The 'supported, 8 per surface' text comes from the unreleased master docs, so decal-based puddles and blood must be faked. Two refinements: the official wasm32 templates likely cap memory at 2 GB (Emscripten default MAXIMUM_MEMORY), not 4 GB, and the shadow atlas has no web-specific default. The central recommendation stands: develop and approve every milestone in gl_compatibility from day one, and treat Forward+ as an optional desktop-only extra. Building the Mac app first and exporting to web later is viable only on that basis. Do an early web export to measure performance on Safari, Chrome and Firefox.

research.topic: Proven Godot 4.x techniques for Neon Static gameplay systems under a single-threaded web export (research as of 2026-11-17)
research.summary: Almost everything this game needs can be done in plain GDScript with built-in nodes, and that is the safe path, because the web export is Compatibility-renderer only (WebGL 2), single-threaded by default since 4.3, and cannot use GDExtension addons without a thread-enabled, cross-origin-isolated build. The three biggest traps are: (a) VehicleBody3D is officially "not designed to provide realistic 3D vehicle physics" and has known issues, so use a simple custom arcade car instead; (b) the Compatibility renderer has no SSR, no volumetric fog, no decals, no depth of field, no ubershader/pipeline precompilation and no automatic instancing, so the wet-street look must be faked with a scripted shader/trick, and shader-compile stutter must be handled by hand (show every material/particle for a frame behind a loading screen); (c) LimboAI (best behaviour-tree addon, MIT, current v1.8.1 targeting Godot 4.7.2) is a C++ module/GDExtension with no web asset in its latest release, so web use is unconfirmed and would require the thread/extension export path or a custom engine template. I could not confirm that occlusion culling works in Compatibility or web templates, so treat it as unavailable and rely on frustum culling, visibility ranges, chunking and small districts. Official docs give almost no hard numbers for web performance, so budgets here are conservative guidance and must be profiled in an actual Chrome/Safari web build early. Open-source arcade car options are thin: the best-documented simple route is the KidsCanCode sphere-car recipe (acknowledged unfinished in places), plus a hand-written raycast RigidBody3D; I found no clearly MIT-licensed, actively maintained, tuned-for-arcade Godot 4 raycast car I can recommend with confidence. Saves are straightforward (JSON in user://) and persist on web via IndexedDB, but only if the browser allows it, and private browsing or blocked cookies breaks it, so export/import a save code as a fallback.

findings.point: VehicleBody3D is officially a poor foundation
findings.detail: Godot class docs: the class 'has known issues and isn't designed to provide realistic 3D vehicle physics'; for advanced physics write your own with CharacterBody3D or RigidBody3D. Quirks: do not set position/orientation directly (breaks sim), node origin acts as centre of gravity (keep low), gears ignored, default mass 40 (docs figures assume mass 1000: engine_force about 25-50, brake about 25-30), steering in radians in code. VehicleWheel3D defaults: wheel_friction_slip 10.5 but docs say start at 1.0; suspension_stiffness 5.88; suspension_max_force 6000 (must exceed quarter of body mass, 3-4x quarter-mass works); roll_influence 0.1 (lower tips easily); wheel_rest_length 0.15. Many tuning values interact with mass, so it needs hand tuning by a non-coder via feedback rounds.

findings.point: Jolt is now default physics (4.6) and interacts uncertainly with VehicleBody3D
findings.detail: Official 4.6 release page: Jolt promoted from experimental (added 4.4) to default for new 3D projects; existing projects keep settings; behaviour differs from GodotPhysics (collisions, stacking, joints). The Jolt docs page does not mention VehicleBody3D at all, so Jolt compatibility is unconfirmed by primary sources. Anecdote (forum, Godot 4.7.1): joints attached to a VehicleBody3D drift under Jolt but not under default physics; an itch.io dev said seams between road collision boxes cause bumps with either engine and fixed it with RigidBody3D wheels or CharacterBody3D. I found no primary source on Jolt in web export; one blog claims it is fine, unverified. Test web early.

findings.point: Sphere/'arcade' car is the least-tuning route, but the reference recipe is half-finished
findings.detail: KidsCanCode 4.x recipe: invisible RigidBody3D sphere (radius 1, angular damp 10, gravity scale 5, bounce 0.1), car mesh follows sphere position, forward force applied along mesh facing only when a downward RayCast3D is grounded (acceleration 35), steering rotates the mesh (about 18 degrees, slerp, only above a minimum speed). Known problems on the page: slope-alignment section marked 'FIX THIS', snippets inconsistent (undefined variables), old Godot 3 syntax (interpolate_with), needs orthonormalized() to stop drift, bounce above 0.5 misbehaves. Pros: forgiving, hard to flip, easy for an agent to write. Cons: no real weight transfer or body collision feel; car mesh can clip walls since collision is a sphere (add a box Area/shape for crash detection).

findings.point: Open-source vehicle projects: few vetted options
findings.detail: Dechode/Godot-AdvancedVehicle: MIT, 201 stars, last push 2026-09-28 (GitHub API), described as 'a more advanced vehicle controller', custom RigidBody with raycast suspension; sim-leaning, Godot version not stated on page. kv-vehicle (itch, katfish-whiskers): Godot 4.x addon, engine/drivetrain/diff/ABS, tunable 'arcade to lite-sim', licence not stated on page, last devlog 2024-04-01, so probably stale. RacingGodot: paid ($30 per search snippet) and aimed at Godot 3.5 with Godot 4 'in development'; skip. TheDuckCow godot-road-generator (relevant to traffic): MIT, 1269 stars, last push 2026-11-15. Overall: borrow ideas, do not depend on any addon for the car.

findings.point: Custom raycast RigidBody3D car: more realistic, more tuning
findings.detail: Pattern: RigidBody3D with 4 RayCast3D/ShapeCast3D suspension points applying spring+damper force, lateral grip force to cancel sideslip, drive force on rear/all, plus artificial downforce and anti-roll. It handles jumps, kerbs and collisions properly (good for crashes in a pursuit) but needs many tuned constants. Sources in my search were forum/itch devlogs (anecdote), not primary docs. For a forgiving arcade feel, add: high lateral friction, steering reduced with speed, strong angular damping, self-righting torque, and a speed cap.

findings.point: First-person driving camera and enter/exit are plain scene logic, no addon needed
findings.detail: No official recipe found. Standard approach (my knowledge, not sourced): the player scene is hidden/disabled (process_mode DISABLED, collision off) and a Camera3D in the car at driver eye position becomes current; exit by placing the player at a pre-set exit Marker3D after a ShapeCast3D free-space check. For the filming-while-driving juggle the camera view needs an independent look offset (mouse look limited to a yaw/pitch cone) and body-sway damping so the viewfinder is usable.

findings.point: Use lane splines/waypoint graph for traffic, not NavigationServer3D
findings.detail: Navigation docs describe NavigationServer/agents for walkable-area pathing and avoidance, and AStar3D as a weighted point graph. For roads, a hand-authored or data-file lane graph (points plus connections) with AStar3D for route choice and Path3D/Curve3D (or just interpolation between points) for following is the common approach; devlogs (anecdote) report Path3D/Curve3D easier to manage than loose Marker3D waypoints, and traffic following linear interpolation between waypoints. The godot-road-generator plugin (MIT, active) builds roads on Path3D and generates lane paths with a RoadLaneAgent, but its version support is inconsistent across sources (v0.9.1 for 4.4+ vs README v0.5.1), so check before depending on it.

findings.point: NavigationAgent avoidance gets expensive; avoid for cars
findings.detail: Official docs: avoidance with many agents has significant cost, enable only on agents needing it; max_neighbors and neighbor_distance drive cost (too low makes avoidance unreliable); 3D avoidance costs more than 2D; avoidance ignores region boundaries; path queries each physics frame are costly. Anecdote (forum): 300 NavigationAgent3D was 'terrible', 600 plain Node3D agents similar performance. No web-specific numbers anywhere. For traffic cars use cheap rules: a forward ShapeCast/RayCast for car-ahead gap, slow to match speed, stop at junction nodes by simple reservation flags, and only simulate cars within a radius of the player (despawn/respawn beyond it).

findings.point: Pursuit that stays filmable is a design/script problem, not an engine one
findings.detail: No source covers this; recommended from first principles. Drive the fleeing car along a pre-authored route through the lane graph, with a 'target gap to the player' controller (rubber-banding: speed up when the player is more than N metres behind, slow or take wider turns when too close), keep chasers scripted to trail the fleeing car and not the player, and trigger outcomes (crash at a staged spot, stop at a dead end, escape past a time/distance threshold) from the scripted route rather than emergent physics. Use real physics only for the player's car and for the final crash flourish. This keeps behaviour deterministic enough for an agent to test in headless runs.

findings.point: CharacterBody3D FPS controller is easy; lean/peek and pick-up must be custom
findings.detail: Asset search: expressobits/character-controller is MIT, 437 stars, pushed 2026-03-04, modular FPS controller with walk/crouch/sprint/swim/fly, headbob (listing said Godot 4.1 originally). No MIT GDScript FPS addon I found lists lean; do it yourself by rolling/offsetting a camera pivot with a ShapeCast3D to stop the camera clipping walls. Crouch: swap/resize the CapsuleShape3D and lower camera, with a ceiling check before standing. Pick up and move objects (evidence moving): the usual pattern is a RigidBody3D pulled toward a hold Marker3D by setting linear_velocity each physics frame (my knowledge; not in the sources fetched). A crossing-the-line system hooks naturally onto pickups, Area3D trespass zones and noise events.

findings.point: Cheap three-stage detection works fine in GDScript
findings.detail: Tutorial (single third-party source, Godot 4.3+): check range first (Area3D or distance), then cone via dot product (120 degree FOV, threshold 0.5, range 15 units), then a line-of-sight ray; use 2 to 3 rays (head 1.7 m, chest 1.0, feet 0.1); suspicion 0 to 100 rising about 30 percent per second when seen, decaying 15 percent per second, alert at 100; run the detection on a 0.1 to 0.2 s timer per NPC and stagger them. Extra for this game: scale rise rate by light level (sample the player's light exposure by summing nearby Light3D energy with distance and by crouch/shadow flags rather than reading pixels), noise as events (footsteps radius by speed and surface), and the camcorder light/IR/flash as an explicit risk. Light sampling via viewport pixel readback is a poor fit for web; use analytic light-zone Area3Ds or a distance/energy sum.

findings.point: LimboAI is the best tool but web support is unconfirmed
findings.detail: Latest release v1.8.1 published 2026-08-20, built against Godot 4.7.2-stable (module builds); README compatibility table: 1.8.x GDExtension needs Godot 4.6+ and module needs 4.7. Licence MIT-style (art and demo CC BY 4.0). It is a C++ module or GDExtension; release assets are editor/export-template builds for Linux, Windows, macOS, Android plus a GDExtension zip for 4.6 and notably no web asset. Asset Library listings (older, 4.2/4.3 era) said the GDExtension build supports Web export. Official Godot web docs say GDExtension on web needs Extension Support enabled and cross-origin isolation (threads), and a forum thread (anecdote) says official web templates lack dlink so you may need a custom template. So: possible but risky, and it would force the threaded export path or a custom engine build.

findings.point: Beehave is pure-GDScript-ish, MIT, current for 4.7
findings.detail: bitbrain/beehave: MIT; latest release v2.9.3 published 2026-08-18 targeting Godot 4.7 (fixes lifecycle on load/unload, singleton conflict in 4.7.1, scene duplication). The repo README table is inconsistent with that (says 2.10+ for 4.5+), so check the actual tag. README does not state the codebase is pure GDScript, but it uses GdUnit tests and a script_templates folder, and it is widely known as a GDScript addon, so it should run in web without GDExtension; I did not verify web export directly. Caveat: behaviour trees may be overkill; hand-written enum state machines (patrol, investigate, suspicious, flee, call-police, witness) are simpler for an agent to write and debug and have zero web risk.

findings.point: Retargeting works but needs T-pose and import-time fixes
findings.detail: Official 4.7 docs: on the Skeleton3D in Advanced Import set the bone_map (BoneMap plus SkeletonProfileHumanoid, auto-maps by name pattern, so English standard names work best; magenta/red button flags missing/duplicate/bad parent mappings but does not block import). Reference pose is a T-pose facing +Z. Import options: Remove Tracks (Except Bone Transform, Unimportant Positions, Unmapped Bones), Bone Renamer (Rename Bones, Unique Node), Rest Fixer (Apply Node Transform, Normalize Position Tracks which stores motion_scale, Overwrite Axis, Fix Silhouette with filter and base_height_adjustment). Docs warn Overwrite Axis 'can produce horrible results' if the original rest matters, Fix Silhouette cannot fix very different body shapes, and A-pose models need care at the feet. Animations can be imported as an AnimationLibrary (set glTF import mode to Animation Library, reimport, restart editor) and shared across characters. Use AnimationTree state machine plus blend spaces for locomotion; root motion works but I found only vendor blogs, and one forum report of root motion trouble on 4.2.2.

findings.point: Keep the character count and rig standard to make this tractable
findings.detail: For a solo non-3D creator, pick one humanoid rig (e.g. a CC0 pack in T-pose with standard bone names) and reuse its animations everywhere, varying only meshes/textures per NPC. Skinning is CPU/GPU cost on a single thread: docs advise limiting animated models on screen and pausing animation for distant or off-screen characters with VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D/Enabler3D. Mixamo retargeting specifics and Mixamo licence terms were not covered by sources I opened; verify the licence yourself before shipping a public website.

findings.point: GridMap is fine for a block kit; MultiMesh culls all-or-nothing
findings.detail: GridMap docs: MeshLibrary from a scene of MeshInstance3D children; material must be on the mesh resource, not the node slot; at most one StaticBody3D and one NavigationRegion3D per item; default cell_size 2x2x2; cell_octant_size default 8; GridMap cannot be hidden by layers (is not a VisualInstance3D) and bake_navigation makes a region per cell. It is optimised for tile kits, not arbitrary nodes. MultiMesh docs: individual instances are not culled, visibility is whole-MultiMesh, so split into per-chunk MultiMeshes (the docs suggest this), and visible_instance_count can be tuned. Set transform_format before instance_count. Docs note the page has not been updated for 4.7. A solid web-safe layout: hand-placed or data-file-generated modular building scenes inside chunk scenes (about one city block each), MultiMesh for repeated props (lamps, bins, bollards, rain splashes) per chunk, and chunk load/unload by distance behind a screen cut.

findings.point: Occlusion culling and automatic instancing are not safe bets on web
findings.detail: Occlusion culling docs describe CPU rasterisation with Embree and discuss only Forward+ and Mobile; excluded from baking: MultiMesh, particles, CSG (CSG since 4.4), transparent materials. An older 4.4 docs snippet from a search said occlusion culling is not supported by default in Web export templates due to memory constraints, but I could not find that line on the 4.7 page, so treat web support as unconfirmed. The 3D optimisation page says automatic instancing for shared mesh+material works only in Forward+, not Compatibility. Visibility ranges (HLOD) work on any GeometryInstance3D with Begin/End plus margins; fade modes Self and Dependencies force transparent rendering (costly), Disabled is cheapest. Practical: rely on frustum culling, visibility_range_end on far props, small chunks, merged building meshes, and shared materials/texture atlases.

findings.point: Compatibility light limits and shader-compile stutter are real constraints
findings.detail: Compatibility docs: forward single-pass; 8 OmniLights and 8 SpotLights per mesh by default (raisable), directional lights capped at 8; ReflectionProbes limited to 2 per mesh; shadowed lights use a multi-pass approach; no VoxelGI/SDFGI/SSIL, no light projector textures, no decals, no DoF, no volumetric fog, no SSR; MSAA and SSAA only (no TAA/FXAA/SMAA); 8-bit LDR colour. Pipeline-compile stutter docs: ubershaders/precompilation and the shader baker do not apply to Compatibility or web, so you must show every material, particle system and effect in the view frustum for at least one frame during a loading screen. No official draw-call numbers exist for web; set your own budget (for example a few hundred draw calls, fewer than 8 dynamic lights touching any surface, 1 to 2 shadow-casting lights) and measure in a real web build. Neon should be emissive materials and baked/glow rather than hundreds of real lights.

findings.point: Wet streets must be faked; SSR is unavailable in Compatibility
findings.detail: Supported in Compatibility: fog, SSAO, glow, tonemapping, adjustments, custom full-screen quad post-processing. Not supported: SSR, volumetric fog, decals. Options: (1) cheap: low-roughness, high-specular road material with a fresnel-based sky/cubemap fake reflection and emissive neon smears painted as textures and signs reflected via vertically flipped duplicate geometry/billboards; (2) puddle ripples via a spatial shader using world XZ and TIME; (3) planar reflection via a mirrored Camera3D into a SubViewport (add-ons exist, PlanarReflector-CPP for 4.4+, Mirror3D), which costs a second scene render so expensive on web, use low res and only on the main street; (4) the CC0 godotshaders 'Rain puddles with ripples and reflections' is a full-screen depth-based SSR plus ripple shader with a RENDERER_COMPATIBILITY branch, but ssr_max_travel and ripple_max_radius are high performance cost, and it was not verified in Compatibility or on web. Rain itself: a camera-following GPUParticles3D or CPUParticles3D box of stretched quads (particle trails not supported in Compatibility), with a forum anecdote that web particle shaders cause first-use compile lag. Light cones should be unshaded additive transparent meshes; keep their count low (transparent overdraw).

findings.point: JSON in user:// is simplest; web persists via IndexedDB with caveats
findings.detail: Docs: user:// is guaranteed writable; on Web it is a virtual filesystem stored via IndexedDB. Web export docs: persistence requires allowing cookies (IndexedDB), third-party cookies in an iframe, fails in incognito/private mode, and OS.is_userfs_persistent() can give false positives. A forum anecdote (Godot 4.3) reports saves working in Chrome and Firefox but not Edge. Saving-games docs: JSON is human readable but needs manual conversion for Vector2/Vector3/Color etc.; binary store_var/get_var is smaller; ConfigFile is for settings. Avoid loading user-supplied Resource files in a public site (code-execution risk; my knowledge, not on the fetched page). Recommendation: one versioned JSON dictionary (schema_version, money, reputation, per-station relationships, gear, tapes, day counter, RNG seed), written atomically (write temp then rename, flush/close), plus an 'export save as text code / import' button as a fallback for blocked storage, and a visible warning if persistence cannot be verified.

findings.point: Single-threaded is default and right for a public site; audio and threads have trade-offs
findings.detail: Official: since 4.3 single-thread is the default/preferred, needing no special headers; thread builds need Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy require-corp (or the PWA service-worker workaround), and cannot coexist with third-party embeds/ads. Extension Support also requires cross-origin isolation. Audio defaults to Web Audio 'Sample' playback: low latency without threads but no AudioEffects, reverb, doppler, procedural audio, or reliable positional audio; switching to Stream restores features but adds latency. Forum anecdotes: 3D audio nodes sounding odd and loops breaking in Sample mode, and a 4.4 crash with Sample mode said fixed in 4.5 (unverified). Hence rain ambience, police scanner (a 2D/non-positional bus) and engine loops should be designed for Sample mode or tested in Stream. Safari has more WebGL 2 issues per the docs, so test Chrome and Safari. Web pauses background tabs and requires user interaction before audio and pointer lock.

recommendations: 1 Car: build a custom arcade car as a RigidBody3D (sphere or low-slung box) with a raycast ground check, strong angular damping, speed-sensitive steering and self-righting; write it as one ~200-line GDScript with all tunables as @export vars so the creator can request 'grippier/looser' changes. Do not use VehicleBody3D. Keep the player car and AI cars on different code paths (AI cars can be kinematic along splines).
1 Camera/enter-exit: scene-swap approach (disable player body, activate car camera, exit via free-space-checked Marker3D) with limited mouse-look cone and speed-based camera shake.

2 Traffic/chase: author a lane graph from a data file (points plus connections, JSON) loaded at startup; AStar3D for route choice; cars follow polyline lanes with a ray gap check; limit to roughly 10 to 20 active cars near the player (profile on web); scripted fleeing route with a gap controller for rubber-banding and scripted crash/stop/escape triggers. Skip NavigationAgent3D for vehicles; use NavigationAgent3D only for pedestrians/guards, with avoidance off by default.

3 On-foot: write your own CharacterBody3D FPS controller (crouch via capsule swap, lean via camera pivot plus ShapeCast3D, pickup via velocity-to-hold-point); use expressobits/character-controller (MIT) only as a reference.

4 Stealth: range, then cone dot product, then 1 to 3 raycasts on a staggered 0.1 to 0.2 s timer; 0 to 100 suspicion meter with rise/decay rates; light exposure from light-zone Area3Ds and a crouch/shadow flag; noise as radius events from the player. Expose the meter to the HUD hints.

5 Brains: hand-written enum state machines in GDScript first. Re-evaluate Beehave (MIT, v2.9.3, 4.7) only if trees become unmanageable. Do not adopt LimboAI unless a web test of a thread-enabled export (or a custom engine template) passes, since no web asset is shipped in v1.8.1.

6 Animation: one standard T-pose humanoid rig, animations imported once as an AnimationLibrary, BoneMap with SkeletonProfileHumanoid, AnimationTree state machine with a locomotion blend space; limit visible animated NPCs (about 10 to 15) and pause off-screen ones. Do a one-character retarget pilot before buying packs.

7 City: hand-placed modular building scenes in chunk scenes (one block per chunk), MultiMesh per chunk for props, visibility_range_end for distant stuff with fade mode Disabled, merged/atlased materials, a handful of real lights plus many emissive meshes; GridMap only for repetitive sidewalks/roads if useful. Add a loading screen that shows every material and particle for a frame. Do not plan on occlusion culling until a web-export test proves it.

8 Look: emissive neon plus Glow (supported in Compatibility), fog, a wet-road shader with fake fresnel/cubemap reflection, scrolling ripple normal map, camera-following rain particles, additive unshaded light-cone meshes. Optionally try the CC0 puddle/SSR shader or a low-res planar reflection SubViewport on the hero street, but gate by a quality setting and measure on a base M-series MacBook Air-class browser.

9 Saves: versioned JSON in user://, atomic write, auto-save at end of each job, export/import save code, startup check that warns if storage appears unavailable. Test in Chrome, Safari and Firefox, plus private mode.

Process: make a 'web gate' milestone before any content: a small scene with the arcade car, rain, 8 lights, 20 animated NPC placeholders and a street chunk, exported to web and loaded in Chrome and Safari, to set real draw-call, light and NPC budgets. Install the Godot web export template at that point.
risks: Compatibility renderer has no SSR, decals, DoF, volumetric fog, TAA, or ubershaders; the cyberpunk wet-street look will be cheaper and less glossy than screenshots of Forward+ projects, and the creator must be told early.
Shader/particle compile stutter on web is unavoidable the first time an effect appears (official docs say precompilation does not apply); needs a loading-screen warm-up pass or in-game hitches.

Single-threaded web build means physics, AI, animation and rendering all share one CPU thread; there are no official numbers, so budgets are guesses until measured. Pursuit scenes (fast car, traffic, chasers, rain, post effects) are the likeliest to miss 60 fps on a base laptop.
VehicleBody3D is officially unreliable; Jolt (default since 4.6) behaves differently from GodotPhysics, and I could not confirm Jolt on web or Jolt plus VehicleBody3D from a primary source.
LimboAI and any GDExtension addon may force a threaded web export with cross-origin isolation headers or a custom engine template, which conflicts with simple static hosting and ad/embed use.
Occlusion culling in Compatibility or web templates is unverified; do not rely on it. GridMap and MultiMesh have all-or-nothing culling behaviours that need chunking.
Sample-mode web audio lacks effects/doppler/reliable positional sound; Stream mode adds latency. Police scanner and ambience mix may need rework between desktop and web.
Web save persistence depends on browser settings (cookies/IndexedDB, private mode, Edge anecdote); players can lose a career if storage fails silently.

Open-source arcade vehicle options are thin and several sources are old or unclear on licence (kv-vehicle licence not stated; RacingGodot paid and Godot 3); an agent must write most of the car, and tuning will take several feedback rounds from a non-coder.

Several recommendations (pickup physics, rubber-banding, enter/exit, light sampling) come from general engineering practice rather than a fetched primary source; flagged medium confidence. Some searches used a search tool that summarises pages, and two doc fetches returned 404 (retargeting at an older URL, jolt unsupported-features file), so some claims rest on secondary excerpts.

research.topic: Camcorder viewfinder and footage-scoring system in Godot 4.7 on the Compatibility renderer and the web
research.summary: The signature mechanic is feasible on Compatibility and the web, but only if the design avoids a few features. The cheapest build is one Camera3D whose fov is changed for zoom, plus a full-screen CanvasLayer shader for the camcorder look. A second 3D render into a SubViewport is needed only for the flip-out screen, for thumbnails, or for a "film cam" that differs from the player's eyes. Real depth-of-field is confirmed unavailable on Compatibility: the official docs say "Depth of field blur is only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility". Depth-based fake focus blur is documented as possible, since hint_depth_texture is listed as supported on all renderers, but I found no source or test confirming it on a Godot 4.7 web build. Compatibility uses different NDC depth maths, and a web screen-texture mipmap bug (#91717) lasted from 4.2 until a fix targeted at 4.5. Scoring is cheap CPU work: is_position_in_frustum, unproject_position and a handful of physics raycasts per subject at about 10 Hz. A "clip" should be stored as a compact timeline of sampled metrics plus a few small thumbnails. get_image() is a documented GPU-to-CPU stall and is slow on Compatibility, and no async readback exists there, so keep thumbnails few, small and event-triggered. The unflattering parts are these. Nothing here has been profiled on a web build, so every cost figure is unmeasured. The web export is single-threaded by default (since 4.3). VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D ignores walls. Safari has more WebGL 2 problems than other browsers. Most public photo-scoring writing is about game design, not implementation, and it warns that rigid scoring rubrics frustrate players. Exclusivity and tamper-evidence are my own design proposals, not sourced patterns, and they work only if every important subject is tagged by hand in the world.

findings.point: DOF (CameraAttributes) is confirmed NOT available on Compatibility
findings.detail: The CameraAttributesPractical class page says "Depth of field blur is only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility". The note is repeated on dof_blur_far_enabled and dof_blur_near_enabled. The 4.7 renderer comparison table lists 'Depth of field blur' as Not supported for Compatibility. The same table lists these as unsupported: custom CompositorEffects, compute shaders, a normal/roughness buffer, SSR, SSIL, SDFGI, volumetric fog, decals, debanding, FXAA/TAA and RenderingDevice access. It lists these as supported on Compatibility: glow (a simpler implementation that always uses screen blend mode, with several glow properties having no effect), SSAO, tonemapping, adjustments, depth/height fog and 3D MSAA. Color is RGBA8 low dynamic range and depth is 24-bit without reverse Z. Any focus blur must therefore be a hand-written shader or a faked effect.
findings.source_date: Live 4.7 docs, read 2026-11-17 (4.7 released about 2026-06-18/19 per secondary coverage)

findings.point: Web export is Compatibility-only, WebGL 2.0, and single-threaded by default
findings.detail: The web export page says Godot 4 web exports target WebGL 2.0 with the Compatibility renderer only, and WebGPU is not supported yet. Single-threaded export has been the default since 4.3. It needs no special headers and works on itch.io, Poki and CrazyGames. The multithreaded option needs the 'Thread Support' export option and the COOP/COEP headers (Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp), or the 'Progressive Web App > Enable' service-worker workaround. Safari has WebGL 2.0 issues that other browsers do not have. Mouse capture and fullscreen must be started from an input event callback. user:// persistence uses IndexedDB and fails in private browsing. Occlusion culling is not available in default web templates because of memory limits (Viewport docs). Secondary coverage of 4.7 reports wasm64 export as the main web change and no WebGPU. Treat that as unverified, because the official release page I fetched did not mention it.

findings.point: Zoom should be a Camera3D.fov change plus a CanvasLayer overlay; the SubViewport second render is for specific cases only
findings.detail: Camera3D.fov is vertical by default (keep_aspect = KEEP_HEIGHT), and a default of 75 corresponds to about 107.5 degrees horizontal at 16:9. Zoom factor is tan(base_fov/2) / tan(fov/2). A Camera3D draws on its nearest parent Viewport, and only one camera can be current per viewport. A second view (a flip-out LCD while driving, or thumbnail capture) therefore needs a SubViewport with its own Camera3D. By default a SubViewport shares the parent's World3D, so no scene duplication is needed. The docs give no cost model for extra viewports. They only say that disabling 3D is slightly faster, that render_target_update_mode can be UPDATE_DISABLED, UPDATE_ONCE, UPDATE_WHEN_VISIBLE (the default), UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE or UPDATE_ALWAYS, and that Camera3D.cull_mask plus VisualInstance3D layers can restrict what the second camera draws. The SubViewport minimum size is 2x2 px. A SubViewport that needs shadows needs positional_shadow_atlas_size above 0. Conclusion: a second camera pass re-submits the scene's draw calls, so I expect it to cost roughly one more scene pass, because on Compatibility and web draw calls are the usual limit. That is my inference, and nobody has benchmarked it in the sources I opened.

findings.point: SubViewport performance on web is an unknown with one alarming anecdote
findings.detail: Anecdote (forum, 2025-02-10, Godot 4.3): a user reported framerate collapsing to under 1 FPS in the web export, especially with several SubViewports active, while editor and native builds ran smoothly. The scene was 3D inside a Control UI with multiple SubViewport TextureRects. No cause or fix was given. A community skill page suggests keeping draw calls under about 500 on Compatibility. That is a third-party rule of thumb, not official. Mitigation for Neon Static: use at most one extra SubViewport, keep it small (about 320x180 to 480x270), run it with UPDATE_WHEN_VISIBLE or only while the flip-out screen is up, and use a low-detail cull_mask. Profile a web build early with RenderingServer rendering info (draw calls) and a frame-time overlay.

findings.point: Camcorder look is a CanvasLayer ColorRect shader; use textureLod(...,0.0) with filter_nearest, and avoid non-zero LOD of the screen texture on web
findings.detail: In canvas_item shaders, a sampler2D with hint_screen_texture reads the screen. For 3D it is copied after the opaque pass and before the transparent pass, so a 2D overlay on a CanvasLayer sees the finished frame. Useful built-ins are SCREEN_UV, SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE and TIME (TIME ignores pause but not time scale). Scanlines, grain, chromatic aberration (offset R/G/B samples), vignette and the timestamp (a Label or drawn text, not shader text) are all one pass, with a few texture samples and no mipmaps. Known web bug: GitHub issue #91717 'Blur shader doesn't work in WebGL 2.0' (labels bug, platform:web, topic:rendering): textureLod with LOD above 0 on the screen texture fails on WebGL 2 with 'Attached mip level is invalid for texture' (Firefox) or 'Attachment level is not in the [base level, max level] range' (Chrome). The cause was the backbuffer allocating too few mip levels. It appeared in 4.2.x, not in 4.1.1, and was closed 2025-03-12 by PR #103878 with milestone 4.5. So it should be fixed in 4.7, but I did not verify it on a 4.7 web build. Even so, the safe design is a 5 to 9 tap blur at LOD 0. Docs: with a non-mipmap filter, LOD above 0 looks the same as 0. Bloom or glow can come from WorldEnvironment glow, which Compatibility supports in a simpler form.

findings.point: Depth texture is documented as supported on Compatibility, but needs renderer-specific maths and I found no confirmation on a 4.7 web build
findings.detail: The renderer comparison page says depth texture is supported in all three renderers. The advanced post-processing tutorial gives the reconstruction maths. In Forward+/Mobile (Vulkan NDC) the line is vec3 ndc = vec3(SCREEN_UV * 2.0 - 1.0, depth). In Compatibility (OpenGL NDC, Z -1..1) it is vec3 ndc = vec3(SCREEN_UV, depth) * 2.0 - 1.0. A single shader can branch on CURRENT_RENDERER == RENDERER_COMPATIBILITY. The tutorial's vertex shader uses POSITION = vec4(VERTEX.xy, 1.0, 1.0) (reversed-Z since 4.3). Depth can only be read from the current viewport, not from another viewport. Practical consequence: depth read in the main view works, but a depth-driven blur on a flip-out SubViewport view would have to run inside that SubViewport. Anecdotes: a forum user in 4.3 had a depth shader work in Forward+ but fail in Compatibility because of the NDC difference. One unverified godotshaders.com comment says a depth shader is broken in 4.5 Compatibility. A forum thread dated 2025-11-26 shows depth-texture reads breaking a shader in a web build, but that is Godot 3.5.2 / GLES2, so it does not apply to 4.x. I found no source for MSAA plus depth texture on Compatibility. For a focus effect, an alternative that avoids depth entirely is to compute focus in gameplay: the focus distance is the distance to the raycast hit under the reticle, and blur the screen toward the edges, or fade subjects by their distance from the focus plane in their own materials via a global shader uniform. This is cheaper and works the same everywhere.

findings.point: Sway is plain code on the camera node, no engine support needed, and it should also feed the score
findings.detail: Use FastNoiseLite (noise_type default TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH, frequency default 0.01, seed default 0) sampled over time for 2 to 3 offset channels, or sums of sines, applied to the camera's rotation, with amplitude scaled by zoom (a narrower fov amplifies shake), by movement and by stamina. The sway amount should be stored per sample as a 'steadiness' metric. The docs I fetched do not describe the Noise sampling methods themselves (they sit on the Noise parent class), so confirm the get_noise_1d/get_noise_2d signatures in the build. The player's mouse-look must stay unshaken while only the film camera shakes, otherwise aiming at the target gets frustrating. Physics-interpolation docs warn that interpolation adds input lag and that teleports need care, so keep the camera on the render frame.

findings.point: Camera3D gives point and projection tests; none of them know about occlusion
findings.detail: Camera3D.is_position_in_frustum(world_point) tests a point. is_position_behind(world_point) can return false for a point still outside the field of view. unproject_position(world_point) returns coordinates in the Viewport rectangle and the docs advise calling is_position_behind first, because points behind the camera project to garbage. get_frustum() returns six planes (near, far, left, top, right, bottom) for plane tests. get_camera_projection() needs the camera in the tree. For subject size and centring: project the 8 AABB corners (MeshInstance3D.get_aabb transformed to world space), skip or clamp those behind the camera, take the 2D bounding rect, clip it to the viewport rect, and compute rect_area / viewport_area for size and the offset of the rect centre from the reticle or viewport centre for centring. This is my construction. A forum answer proposes the same idea and I found no built-in 'screen coverage' function. Caveat: an AABB rect overestimates the coverage of thin or irregular shapes (a person is about 40% of their box), so use a per-subject fill factor or project the body's sample points instead.
findings.source_date: Docs live 2026-11; forum thread undated in my read

findings.point: VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D is a coarse frustum-only tool; use it only to wake up subjects
findings.detail: Per the 4.7 docs it is a box that emits screen_entered when any part is visible and screen_exited when none is. It uses an approximate heuristic that does not account for walls or other occlusion unless occlusion culling is used. Occlusion culling is not supported in default web templates (Viewport docs), so in the web build it will effectively ignore walls. is_on_screen() is false for the first frame after entering the tree. It requires visible = true and applies to the camera that renders the frame, so a second SubViewport camera can confuse it (forum anecdote; the official page is silent on multiple cameras). VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D is the version that switches a node's processing on and off. Use it to disable AI and per-subject scoring work for subjects far from the player, and run the exact checks (frustum, rays) for subjects that pass.

findings.point: Cast several rays per subject, from _physics_process, and exclude the player
findings.detail: The ray-casting docs say direct_space_state is only safe to access in Node._physics_process (the space is locked elsewhere), so run queries there even when triggered by input or a timer. PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(from, to, collision_mask, exclude) with the player's RID in exclude. The result is a Dictionary with collider, position, normal, rid and so on, and is empty on no hit. A single centre ray fails for partly hidden subjects (forum anecdote). Use 5 to 9 Marker3D sample points per subject (head, chest, hips, feet, left/right shoulders) and compute visible_fraction = visible_points / total_points, where a point counts only if it is inside the frustum, on screen (unproject within the rect) and its ray reaches the subject's collider first. Give subjects a dedicated collision layer plus a layer for blockers (walls, cars, fences) so glass or fences can be treated as a partial blocker. Cost: for example 10 subjects x 7 rays x 10 Hz = 700 rays/s. That is small for a physics engine on desktop, but the web build is single-threaded and I found no measured numbers, so budget it and stagger subjects round-robin. Also note that the servers docs warn that calls that return values from servers can stall them if used heavily every frame.

findings.point: Sample at about 10 Hz plus on-event, not per frame
findings.detail: My recommendation, not a sourced number: a 10 Hz timer (0.1 s) driven from _physics_process gives 600 samples per minute of tape, which is plenty for seconds-in-frame and smooth curves. Add forced samples on key beats (gunshot, crash, door opens) from the incident script. Skip all work when not recording. When a subject is off-screen per the notifier, skip it. The Godot docs themselves recommend limiting per-frame work, and the physics-tick rate (60 by default) is the ceiling for raycasts.

findings.point: Store a clip as a sample timeline plus a few thumbnails, never video
findings.detail: Per-sample row of about 12 floats (time, camera pos/yaw, fov, focus_distance, steadiness, and per-primary-subject visible_fraction, screen_area, centre_offset, distance, plus a drama value) in PackedFloat32Array. A 120 s tape at 10 Hz is about 1200 rows; at 12 floats of 4 bytes that is about 58 KB (arithmetic, not a measurement). Event list in parallel (time, type, subject_id, payload). Thumbnails: 6 to 12 per tape at 256x144 or smaller, kept as Image via Image.save_jpg_to_buffer(quality = 0.75 by default) or save_webp_to_buffer (lossy option). Image.resize supports INTERPOLATE_NEAREST/BILINEAR/CUBIC/TRILINEAR/LANCZOS, and Lanczos is slowest. The estimate of 10 to 20 KB per thumbnail JPEG is mine and unmeasured. Persist via user:// (IndexedDB on web, which fails in private browsing). Replay at the news desk as a montage: play the thumbnails as stills in an old-TV shell with the metric graph and 'highlight' captions. A fuller option is a 'ghost replay' that records transforms of the camera and key subjects at 10 Hz and replays them in the same scene with animation states. That is feasible because the world is yours, but it is a larger build and would not capture particle state or rain.

findings.point: get_texture().get_image() works but is a documented GPU stall; on Compatibility it is slow and has no async alternative
findings.detail: Texture2D.get_image docs: 'This will fetch the texture data from the GPU, which might cause performance problems when overused.' and 'Avoid calling get_image() every frame, especially on large textures.' A new Image is created on each call. ViewportTexture docs call the ImageTexture conversion 'a slow operation'. Viewport docs: reading the texture too early returns black or outdated data, so await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw first. The renderer table lists RenderingDevice access as unsupported on Compatibility, so there is no async GPU readback route (anecdote: forum users say there is no better option than get_image for this). Anecdote (forum, 2025-04-10, Godot 4.4.1): calling get_image() on every click cost about 3 to 4 seconds per click on Compatibility versus fast on Forward+. Caching the image fixed it. That example was reading a large loaded texture, not a viewport. Another anecdote (godotforums, undated) reports viewport textures giving inconsistent results only in web exports. Nobody I found published numbers for a small viewport capture on a web build. Plan: capture from a small SubViewport (about 256x144 to 320x180) or downscale, do it at most about once per second and only on events or highlights, and measure on web before committing.

findings.point: Public photo-scoring games use a short, recognisable set of criteria; the design press warns about rigid rubrics
findings.detail: Generic patterns, from public descriptions of Pokémon Snap-style systems: subject size in frame, how centred or placed it is, direction/orientation toward the camera, the subject's pose or action, a rarity or special-moment bonus (kept separate from the numeric score in New Pokémon Snap, as a star tier), and bonuses for multiple subjects in one frame. Game Developer article by Michelle Olson (2024-09-16): rule of thirds, centring and size are measurable but scoring can make photography feel like client work, rewards one ideal composition per subject, and makes players discard shots they like. Alternatives it describes: behaviour or action capture (what was captured, not how well), letting players pick favourites, and low-judgment collection. A wildlife photo critic (non-game) treats dead-centre placement as a weakness, so centring bonuses are a design choice, not truth. For Neon Static this argues for a score built mainly from news value (what happened, was it clear, was it exclusive) over pure aesthetics. I did not copy any specific game's content.

findings.point: Make exclusivity a measurable comparison against rival crews and a world 'coverage ledger'
findings.detail: My proposal, not a sourced pattern. Run the same visibility function (frustum plus multi-point rays) from rival stringers' cameras and from fixed cameras (CCTV, police bodycams, traffic helicopter) to build a per-incident coverage ledger of seconds in which each key moment was seen by anyone. Exclusivity for the player's clip = share of the clip's key-moment seconds that no rival crew covered, plus a bonus for first-to-air (clip sold before the rival's footage reaches the same station, using a world clock) and for unique vantage (angle difference from the rivals' positions above a threshold). Rival crews can be cheap scripted agents, a handful per incident, so the extra ray cost is small. Show it to the player as a station 'we have it exclusively / others have it' line in the verdict. The risk is balance: if the ledger is too transparent, the player plays the ledger instead of the incident.

findings.point: Drama is an authored curve per incident multiplied by how well it was captured
findings.detail: My proposal. Each incident script publishes drama_intensity(t) in 0..1 (calm, tension, shots fired, crash, arrest) and flags peak moments with a type and a time window. The player's drama score = integral over the tape of drama_intensity(t) x capture_quality(t), where capture_quality combines visible_fraction, steadiness, subject size and focus (all 0..1). Peak-moment captured = a boolean per authored beat when capture_quality at the beat exceeds a threshold. Optional modifiers: audio loudness bus level and crowd reaction. Because the curve is authored per incident, it is cheap to compute and hard to cheat by filming nothing. Honest downside: authored curves mean every incident type needs hand-tuned beats, and procedural incidents need a drama generator.

findings.point: Track provenance of world objects and expose a 'tamper exposure' metric from the same visibility pipeline
findings.detail: My proposal. Every tamperable object (evidence, a door, a vehicle, a bystander) carries tamper_state (original, moved, added, removed), original_transform and tamper_time. The visibility function that scores subjects also runs for these objects, accumulating tamper_exposure_s (seconds in frame with a visible_fraction above a threshold) and flags the first frame at which it is visible. The player's own visibility is measured the same way if they pass in front of the lens, with their shadow ignored. The consequence system then uses the exposure: (a) in the news-desk verdict, an 'authenticity' score is reduced by exposure x severity of the tamper type; (b) discovery risk grows if rival footage or CCTV from the ledger captured the object's original state (a before/after mismatch); (c) the station's legal desk can reject or demand a retake. Provide several tamper options with different footprints (moving an object leaves a visible gap or disturbed state, staging a prop leaves a mismatch with police reports) so choices are not one-dimensional. Risk: players will expect the camera to 'see' subtle evidence that only exists as flags, so evidence needs visible shader states (scuffs, wet footprints) to feel fair.

recommendations: Main view: one player Camera3D, with zoom as a fov change (clamped, for example 70 down to 12 degrees) eased with a spring. Put a CanvasLayer on top with a ColorRect and one canvas_item shader (hint_screen_texture, filter_nearest, textureLod(...,0.0)) for scanlines, grain, chromatic aberration, vignette and a flicker, plus Label nodes for REC, battery, tape counter and the timestamp. This works on desktop and web, with the one screen copy the docs describe as the cost.

Do not build the second-render SubViewport until the first playable proves it is needed. When it is, make it a small flip-out LCD (about 320x180 to 480x270) with its own Camera3D, a restricted cull_mask and a non-zero shadow atlas only if shadows are needed, and update it only while the screen is visible. Profile draw calls and frame time on the web build before and after adding it.

Fake focus rather than depending on depth: set focus_distance from a ray under the reticle (the clip's focus metric uses the same value), then blur by that, either through a depth-texture shader branched on CURRENT_RENDERER == RENDERER_COMPATIBILITY, or through per-material global shader uniforms. Build and run a tiny depth-texture test scene on a 4.7 web export in Chrome, Firefox and Safari before relying on it.

Build a SubjectTag node (id, kind, importance 0..1, rarity, 5 to 9 Marker3D sample points, AABB, fill factor, tags such as person, plate, face, evidence). Scoring is a single autoload (ClipRecorder) that runs at 10 Hz from _physics_process only while recording, uses VisibleOnScreenEnabler3D to skip far subjects, and stores rows in PackedFloat32Array plus an event list.

Store clips as sample timeline + events + 6 to 12 small thumbnails (256x144, JPEG or lossy WebP) taken with await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw from a small viewport at most about once per second and only on events. Replay at the news desk as a thumbnail montage with a metric graph. Postpone ghost replay (recorded transforms) until the core loop is fun.

Score for news value more than aesthetics: Clip score = key-moment coverage x clarity x exclusivity x authenticity, with framing details (size, centring) as a modifier, not the main term, to avoid the one-ideal-composition complaint in the design literature. Show hints live (reticle tinting, subject-in-frame indicator) and the verdict later, as decided.

Make the whole scoring pipeline a pure function of (timeline, events, ledger, tamper log) so you can unit-test it headless with synthetic tapes, and so the tuning can be changed after play-testing without touching the recorder.

Treat every cost number here as a hypothesis. Add a debug overlay early (FPS, draw calls, ray count per second, capture ms) and make the first web export of a camera-test scene a milestone, because that is where the unknowns (SubViewport cost, get_image on web, depth texture) get answered.
risks: No benchmark found for a second SubViewport render or for a get_image() of a viewport on a Compatibility web build. The only data point is an anecdote of under 1 FPS with several SubViewports in a web export (Godot 4.3, 2025). The cost of the flip-out screen on weak laptops is unknown.

Depth-texture based focus blur is documented as supported on Compatibility but I found no confirmation on a 4.7 web build. Compatibility uses different NDC maths, and there is an unverified report of a depth shader breaking in 4.5 Compatibility.

Screen-texture shaders on web have had real bugs (issue #91717: textureLod above 0 failed on WebGL 2 from 4.2). It was closed as fixed for 4.5, but should still be re-tested in 4.7 on Chrome, Firefox and Safari; Safari has more WebGL 2 issues in general.
No async readback on Compatibility, so frame capture stalls the GPU. Too many or too large thumbnails will cause visible hitches at the exact moment of action.

VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D and the physics-free frustum tests ignore occlusion and web has no occlusion culling by default, so correctness depends on your own raycasts and well-placed sample points. Glass, fences, rain and smoke will make 'visible' ambiguous.
The web build is single-threaded by default (since 4.3). Raycasts, scoring and AI share one thread with rendering, so the scoring budget must be small. Ray counts must be capped and staggered.

A rigid scoring rubric can make filming feel like client work and reward one 'correct' shot, which is the exact complaint in the design press. Exclusivity, drama and tamper evidence are my design proposals, not tested patterns, and they require authored incident data (drama curves, tagged objects, rival coverage) for every incident type.
Bounding-box coverage overestimates how much of a person is in frame, and a zoomed-in shake can make the metrics noisy. Smoothing and thresholds will need play-test tuning.

Most evidence is from live 4.7 docs (undated living pages) and 2024 to 2025 forum threads on 4.2 to 4.4. Anecdotes are labelled as such. Some 4.7-specific behaviour could differ, and secondary coverage of the 4.7 release (wasm64, HDR) was not confirmed on the official release page.

research.topic: Agent-driven build, run and test of a Godot 4.7 game (CLI, tests, bots, perf, MCP, web export, multi-agent hygiene, AI-GDScript pitfalls)
research.summary: An AI agent in a terminal can do a lot without a human: parse-check scripts, import, run unit tests (GUT or gdUnit4, both MIT, both advertise 4.7 support), run deterministic headless simulations, export, and report numbers as JSON. What it cannot do headlessly is see pixels. Godot 4's --headless uses a dummy renderer, so screenshots, render stats and shader/look checks need a real display driver (a window opens on the Mac), and Godot's web export supports only the Compatibility renderer. That last point is the biggest finding for this project. Develop on Forward+ and the web build will not match: no decals, SSR, SDFGI, volumetric fog, DoF blur or CompositorEffects, and only 8 lights per mesh by default. Pick Compatibility from day one, or accept the app and web builds as two looks. Safari is documented as a weak WebGL2 target. Playwright WebKit on macOS is untested by me and has known pointer-lock and WebGL oddities. The "Godot MCP" scene is crowded, mostly young, and mostly vendor-blogged. The free options add real value mainly for live screenshots and editor-state inspection. Plain CLI scripts cover most of what a terminal agent needs. Recommended shape: many fast headless logic tests, a few scripted bot runs that dump JSON, a small number of windowed screenshot/perf smoke runs, and a web smoke test in headed Chromium. Anything about "feel", the look of the camcorder, and driving feel still needs the human. I could not verify several things (listed under open questions), and some claims come from vendor blogs or forum anecdotes. Those are labelled.

findings.point: godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf is installed and the help text confirms all the key flags exist in this editor build.
findings.detail: `godot --help` shows: --headless (= --display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy), -s/--script, --check-only (use with --script), --quit, --quit-after <int> (iterations), --fixed-fps, --time-scale, --write-movie <file>, --max-fps, --disable-vsync, --disable-render-loop, --log-file, --print-fps, --import, --export-release/--export-debug/--export-pack/--export-patch, --resolution WxH, --position X,Y, --path, --scene, --debug, --gpu-profile, --single-threaded-scene, '--' separator for user args (read via OS.get_cmdline_user_args()). Display drivers listed for this macOS build: macos (vulkan, metal, opengl3, opengl3_angle, dummy) and headless. The help also notes unknown arguments are silently ignored (docs), so typos will not error.

findings.point: --headless is a shortcut for the headless display driver plus the Dummy audio driver; RenderingServer returns dummy values under it.
findings.detail: Docs: --headless is 'required on platforms that do not have GPU access' for export. RenderingServer docs: '--headless disables all rendering and window management functions' and 'most functions return dummy values'. --script must point at a script extending SceneTree or MainLoop. --check-only 'must be used with --script'. --quit-after counts iterations (frames), and 0 disables it. The CLI page documents no exit codes except for --validate-extension-api, so test runners (GUT 0/1, gdUnit4 0/100/101) define their own. Relative --export and --write-movie paths resolve against the project directory, not the shell cwd.

findings.point: --fixed-fps and --time-scale give repeatable stepping, but they do not make the whole game deterministic.
findings.detail: --fixed-fps 'disables real-time synchronization' (frames advance by a fixed delta regardless of wall clock), so a bot can run faster than real time on a headless box. --time-scale scales game time. Physics (Godot Physics 3D) is not documented as bit-deterministic across machines, and random numbers must be seeded in game code (seed(), RandomNumberGenerator.seed). I found no official statement guaranteeing cross-platform determinism, so assert on tolerances and invariants, not exact positions. A car-chase with vehicle physics is the likeliest to drift.

findings.point: Headless cannot produce screenshots; the agent needs a real display driver, which means a window appears on the Mac.
findings.detail: Under --headless the renderer is the Dummy server, so Viewport.get_texture().get_image() returns nothing useful (Ask Godot thread, anecdote: 'I don't have any image'; the Godot 4 docs warn separately that grabbing the viewport texture too early, e.g. in _ready(), gives an empty image, so wait for RenderingServer.frame_post_draw). Recipe: run non-headless (display driver macos), await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw, then get_viewport().get_texture().get_image().save_png(path). I could not confirm whether the window can be kept off-screen/hidden on macOS (--position with off-screen coordinates is untested), so assume a window briefly appears and steals focus. On Linux CI the answer is Xvfb; on this Mac there is no equivalent I verified.
findings.source_date: anecdote, date not shown (Godot 3 to 4 era)

findings.point: --write-movie is a good deterministic frame-capture tool: non-real-time, perfect pacing, PNG sequence or AVI, not headless-documented.
findings.detail: Usage: `godot --path <proj> --write-movie out.avi --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 300`. Extension selects format: .avi (MJPEG + uncompressed audio, fast, 4 GB limit), .png (lossless numbered sequence with 8 digits plus a .wav; needs transparent_bg only for alpha), .ogv (Theora/Vorbis; docs say OGV can only be recorded in editor builds). --write-movie is available in exported projects. Force-stopping (Ctrl+C or F8) can leave an invalid AVI, so always use --quit-after or get_tree().quit(). 'Mix Rate must be divisible by the recorded FPS' to avoid audio desync. The docs do not address headless operation; it needs rendering, so treat it as needing a real display driver. Recording is slow at high resolution; useful for the agent to pull specific frames (extract with ffmpeg, if installed) to inspect the camcorder look.

findings.point: GUT 9.7.1 (godot_4_7 branch) is the version for Godot 4.7; MIT; pure GDScript; headless CLI with JUnit XML.
findings.detail: Releases page: 9.7.1 (10 July, year not shown, presumably 2026) is newest; 9.7.0 notes say 'Compatibility changes for Godot 4.7'; the version table maps 9.7.1 to the godot_4_7 branch and Godot 4.7.x, while the 'Latest'-badged 9.6.1 is for 4.6.x. Note the trap: the GitHub 'Latest' badge points at 9.6.1, not 9.7.1. 9.7.1 notes: GUT now ignores 'Compiler bug: Unresolved return' errors that can appear when generating doubles (the error still prints). Licence MIT (addons/gut/LICENSE.md). No GDExtension dependency is mentioned. CLI (docs): `godot -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -d --path "$PWD" -gdir=res://test/unit -gexit -gjunit_xml_file=results.xml`; use `=` not a space after options (a space caused 'No loader found for resource'). Exit code 0 on all pass, 1 on any failure; pending tests do not affect it. Add --headless for no window. GUT docs did not state a requirement to run --import first; in practice do it (see item 8).

findings.point: gdUnit4 supports 4.7 on its 6.2.x line and master (v7.0.0); MIT; also has C# support but needs no GDExtension for GDScript.
findings.detail: README compat table: master (v7.0.0) = Godot 4.7, 4.7.1, 4.8.dev7; v6.2.x = 4.5 through 4.7.1; v6.1.x = 4.5 to 4.6.3. Newest release shown: v6.2.3 (1 Nov, year not shown) which 'fixes a font size error on a fresh Godot 4.7 editor'. Our installed 4.7.2 is not listed explicitly (4.7.1 is), so expect it to work but verify. Licence MIT. CLI: `GODOT_BIN=/path/to/godot ./addons/gdUnit4/runtest.sh -a ./test` (flags: -a add path, -i ignore, -c continue after first failure, -conf, -rd report dir default res://reports/, -rc report count default 20). Exit codes 0 pass, 100 failures, 101 warnings. Outputs index.htm and results.xml (JUnit) per run. The two docs pages I opened did not cover headless caveats or whether --import must precede it, so I cannot confirm those. Unflattering: the runner stops at the first failure unless -c is given. Both frameworks support scene-runner style tests; gdUnit4 has a more featureful scene runner (input simulation, await signals), GUT is lighter.

findings.point: Input can be simulated in-process with two different mechanisms that behave differently; a bot should use both deliberately.
findings.detail: Input.action_press(action, strength) sets state for is_action_pressed/just_pressed but 'does not trigger _input() calls' (docs). Input.parse_input_event(event) feeds an InputEvent through the normal pipeline and does call _input/_unhandled_input, but does not move the OS cursor. With MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED, mouse look reads InputEventMouseMotion.relative, so a bot should synthesise InputEventMouseMotion with relative set. use_accumulated_input (default true) merges motion events per frame; Input.flush_buffered_events() forces delivery. The docs do not say whether parse_input_event works headless; logic-only paths generally do, but I did not verify. Pattern: a bot Node (autoload, enabled only by a user arg read from OS.get_cmdline_user_args(), e.g. `-- --bot=chase_01 --seed=42`) steps through scripted waypoints per physics frame, asserts conditions (player reached zone, was unseen, battery > 0), writes JSON via FileAccess/JSON.stringify to a path from user args, then calls get_tree().quit(code). Run with --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after N as a hard stop. This is my design recommendation; I found no first-party sample for it.

findings.point: Bots can verify logic, reachability and timing; they cannot judge fun, readability of the viewfinder, or driving feel.
findings.detail: Stealth detection, pursuit AI following, scanner-to-incident triggering, tape/battery drain, crossing-the-line penalties and payout maths are all assertable. Whether 'hints live, verdict later' reads well, whether the car is forgiving enough, and whether the neon looks good need a person or at least screenshot review by a model. Expect bots to be brittle around physics-driven car chases (non-deterministic across hardware, per item 1) and navigation meshes.

findings.point: Performance.get_monitor covers FPS, process/physics time, object/node counts, draw calls, primitives, memory, but some monitors are debug-only and render stats are dummy in headless.
findings.detail: Monitor enum (4.7 stable docs): TIME_FPS(0), TIME_PROCESS, TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS, MEMORY_STATIC(4), MEMORY_STATIC_MAX, OBJECT_COUNT(7), OBJECT_RESOURCE_COUNT, OBJECT_NODE_COUNT, OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT(10), RENDER_TOTAL_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME(11), RENDER_TOTAL_PRIMITIVES_IN_FRAME(12), RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME(13), RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED(14), RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED, RENDER_BUFFER_MEM_USED, physics 2D/3D active objects, pairs, islands, AUDIO_OUTPUT_LATENCY(23), navigation counts, and PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_* (34 to 38, useful for shader-stutter hunting). Debug-only caveats stated in docs: MEMORY_STATIC and MEMORY_STATIC_MAX not available in release builds; OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT returns 0 in release; 'some other built-in monitors also return 0 in release exports' (not named). Custom: Performance.add_custom_monitor('Game/ActiveCars', callable); read with get_custom_monitor(id); values must be >= 0. Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_VISIBLE/SHADOW/CANVAS, RENDER_INFO_OBJECTS/PRIMITIVES/DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME) gives per-pass counts (shadow pass objects render multiple times, so shadow-heavy neon streets inflate it). Whether these render counters return real values in a web release export is NOT confirmed; test it early. Note the primitives monitor is labelled 'vertices' in Viewport docs. FPS measured on a dev laptop says little about 'any recent laptop', so log frame time percentiles (1% low) rather than average FPS.

findings.point: JavaScriptBridge lets the web build push perf numbers to the browser console/window, where Playwright can read them.
findings.detail: JavaScriptBridge is 'implemented only in the Web export' (enabled in official templates). JavaScriptBridge.eval(code, true) runs JS in the global context, e.g. `JavaScriptBridge.eval("window.__perf = " + JSON.stringify(stats), true)`, and Playwright then does page.evaluate(() => window.__perf). Plain print() output also reaches the browser console, which Playwright can capture via page.on('console'). Guard all JavaScriptBridge calls with OS.has_feature('web') so desktop runs do not break. The perf-in-web path itself is my recommendation; the docs only confirm the eval/callback API.

findings.point: There is no official Godot MCP; the field is many community servers of uneven maturity, and the best-known free one (Coding-Solo) is the thinnest.
findings.detail: Coding-Solo/godot-mcp (github.com/Coding-Solo/godot-mcp): MIT, 6.7k stars, 542 forks, only 60 commits shown, Node 18+. Tools: launch_editor, run_project, stop_project, get_debug_output, get_godot_version, list_projects, get_project_info, create_scene, add_node, load_sprite, save_scene, export_mesh_library, get_uid, update_project_uids (UID tools need 4.4+). No screenshots or input simulation per its README. Sods2/godot-mcp: MIT, 84 tools in 16 categories, but only 4 stars, 140 commits, no releases; has live-editor tools via a plugin on TCP 127.0.0.1:6008, game-window screenshots via an autoload, test running for GUT/gdUnit4, debugger and profiler tools; claims verified against Godot 4.6.3 and 4.7.2; no input-simulation tool documented. hi-godot/godot-ai: MIT, 3.6k stars, 1,229 commits, 46 tools/120+ operations, requires Godot 4.7+, telemetry on by default (opt-out), self-reported '21,000+ monthly active installs'; I could not confirm input/screenshot tools from its README. Others named in a vendor-run roundup (Flockbay, which sells its own app, so treat as biased, updated 2026-11-02): GDAI MCP (gdaimcp.com, $19 once, closed source), Godot MCP Pro (godot-mcp.abyo.net, $15, '187 tools', 4.4+), GoPeak (HaD0Yun/Gopeak-godot-mcp, MIT), satelliteoflove/godot-mcp (MIT, 4.5+, frame-stepping), Summer Engine MCP. I did not open the vendors' own pages for the paid ones.

findings.point: Marginal for a terminal agent: CLI covers parse/run/test/export; MCP adds live screenshots, editor-state reading and debugger access at the cost of an editor that must stay open.
findings.detail: What MCP uniquely adds: screenshots of the running game inside the editor session, editor scene-tree inspection and live node edits with undo, breakpoints and stack traces. What it costs: the editor process holds the project open (conflicts with headless imports/tests on the same working copy, see item 7), a plugin and a local TCP port to trust, third-party code in a project you do not code-review, and version churn. Sods2 itself notes validation falls back to headless --check-only which 'requires the editor to be closed' and mislabels autoloads as 'Identifier not found'. The Flockbay article admits no tool can judge feel and that hand-editing .tscn is error-prone. Recommendation: start with CLI scripts only; add one MCP (godot-ai is the one actively marketed for 4.7, or Sods2 for the test-runner and screenshot tools) only if live screenshot review proves worth it.

findings.point: Web export supports only the Compatibility (OpenGL/WebGL2) renderer, which lacks several features a neon-rain look leans on.
findings.detail: Docs: Compatibility is the only renderer on web; Forward+ and Mobile are not supported; WebGPU not supported yet. Compatibility does NOT support: SSR, SDFGI, VoxelGI, SSIL, volumetric fog, decals, PCSS soft shadows, light projector textures, CompositorEffects (custom post-processing), depth-of-field blur, particle trails/SDF collision, compute shaders. It DOES support glow, depth/height fog and SSAO (per docs). Lights: 8 OmniLight/SpotLight per mesh by default (adjustable) versus 512 per cluster. Consequence: rainy-street reflections via SSR, decal puddles, volumetric neon haze and DoF-based camcorder focus blur all need alternatives (fake reflection planes/cubemaps, mesh or sprite puddles, cheap fog, shader-based focus/noise on a SubViewport or full-screen quad). The camcorder viewfinder look should be done as a screen-space shader that works in Compatibility. Strongly recommend setting the project to Compatibility from the start, or testing the web export each milestone.

findings.point: Export needs the editor binary, installed web templates, a preset in export_presets.cfg, and an imported project; serve with the right headers only if using threads.
findings.detail: Command: `godot --headless --path <proj> --export-release "Web" <proj>/build/web/index.html` (target dir must exist; preset name must match export_presets.cfg and the editor normally creates that file; I could not confirm a way to author it by hand safely, but docs say it can be committed). Since 4.3 single-threaded export is the default and 'works with more hosts' (itch.io, Poki, CrazyGames), so no special headers are needed for the default. Thread Support needs COOP `same-origin` and COEP `require-corp`, or the PWA service-worker workaround, and a secure context. Keep `index.html` as the main name. The docs say to download serve.py from the Godot repo and run `python serve.py --root .` (I did not verify 4.7 changed this); any static server works for single-threaded, e.g. `python3 -m http.server`. .wasm and .pck should be compressed in hosting (docs: gzip to ~a quarter of wasm size). Export templates on macOS install under ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/<version> (from my knowledge; the exporting docs I fetched do not state it). Currently only the macOS template is installed here, so the web template must be installed via the editor (Editor > Manage Export Templates) before any web test; whether that can be scripted I did not verify.

findings.point: Playwright can drive it, but WebGL2 in headless Chromium on Apple Silicon is a known weak spot, so use headed Chromium; WebKit/Safari is the riskiest target.
findings.detail: Playwright's own suite marks its Chromium WebGL test as a known failure on macOS arm64 ('SwiftShader is not available on macOS-arm64', found via search snippet, I did not open the source). So on the M4, run Chromium headed (real GPU) and read the renderer string from the WebGL debug extension to confirm WebGL2 actually initialised. Software-WebGL flag set documented by Chromium for Linux/CI: --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader-webgl --enable-unsafe-swiftshader (weaker security; untrusted pages only); automatic SwiftShader fallback is deprecated. Godot docs: Safari 'has several issues with WebGL 2.0 support that other browsers don't', recommend Chromium or Firefox; Godot 4.3 progress report: Apple devices' threaded-export problems disappear with single-thread; a forum report of WebGL context loss on iOS 18 (anecdote). WebKit bug reports show pointer lock gaps and WebGL failing on some GitHub macOS runners (bug titles only). Pointer lock and fullscreen need a user-gesture-driven call, and Godot's docs say to do it from _input/_unhandled_input, not by polling Input. Audio needs a prior click/keypress (docs: add a splash 'click to start'). Automation consequence: the test must page.mouse.click() the canvas (real input event) before asserting mouse capture; a headless run can verify load and no console errors but may not grant pointer lock the same way a human click does (unverified). No verified Godot-specific Playwright recipe exists in what I found.

findings.point: I found no evidence Godot protects .godot from two processes writing at once; treat one working copy as single-writer.
findings.detail: Search found no Godot issue or doc on concurrent editor/headless import safety. Closest anecdotes (forum/blog, some look AI-generated): fast close-and-reopen leaves half-written UID cache; fix is delete .godot/ and run `godot --headless --import`. Official docs: add .godot/ to VCS ignore; it 'stores various project cache data'. The docs I fetched say nothing about .uid files, but Godot 4.4 release notes confirm per-script .uid files exist and are fully supported, so commit them. A real, closed Godot bug (issue #86187, Dec 2023, fixed in 4.3 milestone) shows editor resource-cache handling can corrupt .tscn by embedding PackedScenes as sub-resources, which also shows that opening/saving scenes in the editor rewrites files an agent just edited. Flockbay article: saving the editor's copy of an open script overwrites an agent's disk change. Practical rules: one git worktree (or clone) per agent, each with its own .godot (never share a working directory); run `godot --headless --import` once per worktree after checkout and after adding assets; never have the human editor open on the same folder an agent is writing; serialise merges, treat .uid and .import files as committed; keep binary assets in LFS. Cost: a fresh import of a cyberpunk asset pack on each worktree takes time and disk (not measured). Running several game instances at once is fine for runtime, but each loads the same files; avoid two writing to user:// logs or reports at the same path (use unique --log-file and report dirs).

findings.point: Typed GDScript has silent traps: `as` casts return null without error, warnings like untyped/inferred declarations are off by default, and several global math functions are untyped.
findings.detail: From the static typing docs: `as` silently yields null on mismatch (use `is` or assert); typed arrays only constrain some operations (push_back etc. stay untyped); nested typed collections (Array[Array[int]]) unsupported; enums are only ints; UNTYPED_DECLARATION and INFERRED_DECLARATION warnings must be enabled manually (Project Settings > Debug > GDScript, Advanced); UNSAFE_* warnings 'do not cover all cases'; abs/clamp/lerp/round etc. return untyped values, so use clampf/absi/lerpf. Docs show warning-to-error is a per-warning project setting (`debug/gdscript/warnings/<name>`, e.g. unused_variable), warnings are named identically in @warning_ignore. I could not confirm whether --check-only honours warnings-as-errors or whether treat_warnings_as_errors exists. Other well-known failure modes (my knowledge, not verified in this pass): Godot 3 API names (yield, KinematicBody, rand_range, connect string syntax, onready/export without @), changed 4.x names (CharacterBody3D.velocity/move_and_slide(), set_surface_override_material, Tween via create_tween), `:=` on a Variant fails to infer, and hand-edited .tscn files with wrong load_steps, duplicate/missing ext_resource ids or fabricated uid:// strings. Flockbay article: hand-editing .tscn is error-prone because resource IDs and UIDs are easy to get wrong. Best practice: have the agent build scenes in GDScript or via small generator scripts using PackedScene.pack() rather than typing .tscn text.

findings.point: gdtoolkit (gdlint, gdformat) is MIT, but its last release found is 4.5.0 on 9 Oct 2025, so 4.7 syntax coverage is unproven.
findings.detail: PyPI: 4.5.0 (Oct 9, 2025), 4.3.4 (Jun 29, 2025), 4.3.3 (Nov 2, 2024); needs Python >= 3.7; README installs with `pip3 install "gdtoolkit==4.*"`. Tools: gdlint, gdformat (README warns of possible data loss, use git), gdparse, gdradon. It is a separate Python parser, not Godot's, so new syntax (e.g. 4.5 variadic args or abstract classes, if used) may be rejected as parse errors (my inference; not tested). Use gdlint as advisory and Godot's own --check-only as the authority. Do not auto-run gdformat on the whole repo without checking it round-trips on a sample.

findings.point: --check-only needs --script and parses one script at a time, so a project-wide check requires a loop or a custom validator script plus a prior import.
findings.detail: Docs: `--check-only` 'Only parse for errors and quit (use with --script)'. It does not by itself resolve every cross-script reference or autoload (Sods2 notes autoloads show as 'Identifier not found'). A stronger guard is a headless smoke script that loads every .tscn/.gd via ResourceLoader.load() and instantiates scenes, printing errors and exiting non-zero. Always run `godot --headless --path <proj> --import` before tests or export on a fresh checkout so .godot/imported exists (the import flag implies --editor and --quit per docs). Godot prints script errors to stdout/stderr but returns exit code 0 in many cases, so wrappers must grep the log for 'ERROR:' / 'SCRIPT ERROR:' / 'Parse Error' and fail the step (my experience; the CLI docs list no exit codes for these flags).

recommendations: Decide the renderer now: set the project to Compatibility from day one (the only web-capable renderer) and design the look within it (fake reflections/puddles, glow, fog, SSAO, shader-based camcorder noise and focus blur). Otherwise the web export will look noticeably worse than the Mac app and the creator will be surprised late.

Test pyramid, base: fast headless logic tests in GUT 9.7.1 (godot_4_7 branch) or gdUnit4 6.2.x. Pick one framework. GUT is the lighter, simpler CLI and returns 0/1. gdUnit4 gives HTML and JUnit reports and a richer scene runner but needs the `-c` flag to run past the first failure and uses 0/100/101 exit codes. Test pure code: payout maths, reputation, crossing-the-line rules, scanner-to-incident scheduling, battery/tape state, detection scoring.
