Test pyramid, second layer: scripted bot runs, headless where possible, with --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after N and a bot autoload enabled by user args after `--`. Each run asserts game state and writes a JSON report (seed, waypoints reached, detected or not, time, score), then quits with a non-zero exit code on failure. Use parse_input_event for mouse-look and _input paths and action_press for polled actions. Use tolerances, not exact positions, for vehicle physics.

Test pyramid, third layer: windowed smoke runs (non-headless, macOS display driver) that await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw, save PNG screenshots from a list of fixed camera positions, and log Performance monitors plus Viewport.get_render_info as JSON. Use --write-movie PNG or AVI sequences for short fixed-frame captures. A model can review the images against a checklist of what each shot should contain. Expect a window to appear on the Mac and treat these runs as slower, less frequent gates.

Test pyramid, top: a web smoke test with Playwright in headed Chromium. Steps: serve the export (python3 -m http.server is enough for the default single-threaded build), load, click the canvas for the audio/pointer-lock gesture, capture console messages and page errors, read window.__perf (set from GDScript via JavaScriptBridge.eval), take a canvas screenshot, record time-to-first-frame. Fail on any console error. Add a WebKit run as an advisory check only, not a gate, until it is proven to work on this M4. Install the Godot web export template before the first web build; only macOS is installed now.

Guard rails to wire into one script (e.g. tools/check.sh): git status clean-ish, `godot --headless --path . --import`, per-file `godot --headless --check-only --script <file>` over all .gd (or a validator script that loads every scene and script), gdlint as advisory, then the unit tests; wrap Godot calls with a log grep for 'ERROR:', 'SCRIPT ERROR:' and 'Parse Error' and fail on a match because exit codes are not reliable.

Turn on strictness in project.godot early: enable UNTYPED_DECLARATION, INFERRED_DECLARATION or the UNSAFE_* warnings and set the ones you care about as errors via debug/gdscript/warnings/<name>; require static typing in the agent instructions; ban `as` casts without a following null check; require clampf/lerpf/absi style typed helpers.

Make the agent generate scenes with GDScript builder scripts that call PackedScene.pack() or small helper functions, and avoid hand-typed .tscn text; if .tscn must be edited, require a load-and-instantiate check right after. Commit .uid files and .import files; ignore .godot/.

Multi-agent setup: one git worktree per agent, each with its own .godot, import once per worktree, a single integration worktree that runs the full check script, and no human editor open on a folder an agent is writing to. Give every parallel run a unique --log-file, report dir and bot-report path. Start with at most two or three agents until the import and disk cost is known.

MCP: start without one. If live screenshots or editor-tree inspection prove necessary, trial Sods2/godot-mcp (test runner, game screenshots, MIT, claims 4.7.2 verified, but very low adoption) or hi-godot/godot-ai (MIT, 4.7+, much larger user base) in a throwaway copy of the project, and read the plugin code before enabling it. Avoid paying for closed-source options until a free one fails a concrete need. Disable telemetry in godot-ai if used.

Keep a short human playtest checklist (look, feel, readability of hints, car forgiveness, stealth tension) per milestone; automate only what has a pass/fail answer. Do not claim a milestone is 'passed' on bot results alone.
risks: Renderer gap: developing on Forward+ then discovering the web build lacks decals, SSR, DoF blur, volumetric fog and CompositorEffects, with only 8 lights per mesh by default. This can force a late art and shader rework.

Headless cannot screenshot or measure rendering. The agent's picture of 'what it looks like' depends on non-headless runs that open a window on the Mac, and I could not confirm any way to keep that window hidden.

Safari and WebKit are the documented weak spot for Godot web exports (WebGL2 issues, historic memory reloads, iOS 18 context-loss report). A 'free public website' will hit Safari users; the only mitigation is early and repeated testing, and possibly telling Safari users to expect problems.

Playwright on Apple Silicon: Chromium headless WebGL is a known gap (SwiftShader unavailable on macOS arm64, per a Playwright test annotation seen in search results), so automated web tests need headed browsers, which are slower and steal focus. Pointer-lock behaviour in automation is unverified.
Determinism: physics-driven chase scenes may differ across runs and machines, so flaky bot tests are likely; the answer is tolerances and many seeds, not exact asserts.
Godot exit codes cannot be trusted for script errors; a green exit with 'SCRIPT ERROR' in the log is plausible. The wrapper must grep logs.

Tool maturity: Sods2/godot-mcp has 4 stars and no releases; godot-ai's adoption numbers are self-reported telemetry; most MCP comparisons come from vendors selling their own tools. gdtoolkit's last release is Oct 2025 and may not parse newer syntax.
Shared .godot and the editor rewrite files: concurrent editor/import use on one folder is unsupported as far as I found, and editor saves can overwrite agent edits on disk.

Release-build monitors: several Performance monitors return 0 in release exports, and I have not confirmed which render counters work in a web release build, so web performance numbers may need a different measurement path (frame time via _process delta, plus browser performance tools).
Cost and time of import: every worktree needs its own import of the asset packs and AI-generated models; the size of this was not measured.

research.topic: Asset shopping list and licences for a free public web build of a stylized low-poly cyberpunk night-city game (Godot 4.7, GLB/FBX)
research.summary: No single publisher covers everything. Synty POLYGON is the only family that credibly covers most of the list with one art style: the City Pack ($9.99 sale / $19.99 list) and Sci-Fi City ($25 sale / $49.99 list) both list a native Godot project plus FBX. Both list cars, characters, props, and modular buildings. Synty's own FAQ still says only Unity and Unreal are officially supported, and several store pages showed "Sold out" and 429 errors, so verify live. Synty's licence allows shipping assets inside a game and bars sharing source files outside your team. It says nothing about web builds, and a web build puts the assets in a downloadable package, so email Synty before shipping. Kenney (City Kit Roads, Car Kit; CC0, confirmed vehicles, no police car confirmed) and Quaternius (CC0; Downtown City MegaKit, Universal Animation Library, Universal Base Characters) are the zero-risk licence options. They cost nothing, need no attribution, and carry no web-build redistribution question, but they are not cyberpunk and they use different art styles from Synty and from each other. Real gaps remain after any pack choice. I found no confirmed police car, police officer, masked robber, convenience-store interior, police tape, evidence markers, or camcorder model in a licence-clean low-poly set. The camcorder is mostly viewfinder UI anyway. A convenience store has only unverified candidates, and the in-world neon signs, wet-street look, and camcorder UI can be built in Godot with emission, glow, and shaders. Mixamo (Adobe) is allowed in games but forbids distributing raw files, and a web build ships them. For AI 3D models, free tiers are CC BY 4.0 (Meshy) or non-commercial (Tripo), so a paid month on one generator is required. Hunyuan3D's licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea, which makes it a poor choice for a public web game. For scanner voices, Kokoro (Apache 2.0) is the cleanest TTS route; Piper voices need per-voice chain checks, and ElevenLabs free output is non-commercial. Recording yourself with a radio filter is the safest option of all.

findings.point: Synty POLYGON is the closest to one coherent family, with Godot projects in two packs.
findings.detail: POLYGON City Pack: $9.99 shown on sale (list $19.99), Godot 4.5.1 project + Unity + Unreal + FBX, 331 unique assets, 8 cars with 12 variations each, 9 characters (4 colours, 3 skin tones each). POLYGON Sci-Fi City: $25.00 on sale (list $49.99), Godot 4.6.2 project + FBX, 509 unique assets, 24 alt colour textures, characters/props/weapons/vehicles/modular environment. Both pages showed 'Sold out' next to the sale price, so availability and price need a live check. Flat-colour palette-texture low-poly style; I found no polycount figures. Synty's FAQ says only Unity and Unreal are officially supported and Godot is 'technically possible', so treat the Godot projects as new/less proven.

findings.point: Synty's One Time Purchase licence permits shipping in a game; it is silent on web builds; raw files must stay inside your team.
findings.detail: Allowed: assets 'incorporated into Products' under your control, 'to publish, distribute, transmit... and play'; not limited by engine, OS, platform or device. Forbidden: distributing as stock art, sharing source files outside your team, uploading models to third-party 3D-generation services, using in generative-AI datasets or generating 3D models with generative AI, NFT/metaverse use. No attribution required, but you must not claim you created them. The EULA does not mention web/online games. A Godot web build packs assets into a .pck that anyone can open, so the 'don't share source files' clause is a real grey area. Ask Synty support in writing before release. Licence is per 'Team' (5 seats per purchase), and non-transferable. Subscription (All Access) licence only covers dev use while subscribed; the one-time purchase is safer for a long-lived game.

findings.point: Synty's closest cyberpunk pack, Sci-Fi Cyber City, is $199.99 and has no Godot project listed.
findings.detail: POLYGON Sci-Fi Cyber City: $199.99 (5 seats), Unity 2022.3 package + Unreal 5.3 project + FBX only; 157 buildings, 413 props, 19 characters (cyborgs, mercenaries, 'Street Male', rich male/female), 29 weapons, 13 vehicle items (luxury car, SUV, truck, food truck). Grime-soaked low-poly cyber city with modular buildings. For Godot you would use the FBX and rebuild materials yourself (a community converter exists but is unofficial). Vehicles are not ordinary sedans or police cars. Expensive for a free game; the cheaper Sci-Fi City ($25 sale) plus emissive neon in Godot is likely enough.

findings.point: Synty has Shops, Heist and Shop Interiors packs, but Godot support, police content and exact contents are unconfirmed.
findings.detail: POLYGON Heist Pack: 251 unique assets, 25 masks, 22 interior+exterior walls, money notes/stacks x12, jewellery x10, modular bank atrium; Unity Asset Store price $29.99; a user review says it lacks exterior buildings. Masks and cash are directly useful for robbers. POLYGON Shops Pack: Unity Asset Store $99.99 (list $199.99), v1.6.5 May 2026. SIMPLE Shop Interiors (cartoon style, different look): $19.99 on Synty store. I could not confirm Godot projects, police characters, police cars, or a convenience store interior for any of these (the Synty store rate-limited me). Verify on the store page before buying.

findings.point: Kenney City Kit (Roads, Commercial, Suburban) and Car Kit are CC0 with glTF/FBX/OBJ.
findings.detail: Kenney lists CC0 (use anywhere, no attribution needed). City Kit Roads: 90 files, 65+ models, OBJ/FBX/DAE/STL/glTF, includes road signs, traffic lights (v2.1), dumpster. City Kit Commercial (CC0, 50 files) and Suburban (35+ models). Car Kit v2.0 (May 2024): 40+ models (cars, trucks, vans), OBJ/FBX/glTF, 8 separate wheel models per OpenGameArt listing; a mirror lists a 'Police' model but I could not confirm it on Kenney's page. Style is simple flat-colour, very low poly, tidy but toy-like and much plainer than Synty or any cyberpunk look. Kenney page fetches omit format and count details, which come from itch.io and mirrors. No file formats or counts were extractable from kenney.nl itself.

findings.point: Quaternius CC0 packs give a city set, a universal character rig and 120+ animations; base downloads are free.
findings.detail: Downtown City MegaKit: 315 models, FBX/glTF/Blend, CC0, standard free (about 60-70% of pack), paid Source adds Godot/Unity/Unreal projects; prices are shown only as images. Universal Animation Library (v1): 120+ animations on one humanoid rig, locomotion in 8 directions, jog, sprint, crawl, death, combat/gun, emotes; Standard free (45 animations on itch, per page), Source from $14.99; CC0; Godot-store entry says Standard-1.0 updated 2026-06-10 and marked unstable. UAL2: 130+ animations, Standard 'name your price' (free at $0, 42 free), Source $14.99+, explicit Godot exports. Neither page names idle, crouch, aim, hands up or fall clips; confirm in the download before relying on them. Universal Base Characters: 6 base bodies (about 13k tris average, which is not 'low poly' by Synty standards), 20 hairstyles, CC0, no clothing mentioned. 'Cyberpunk Game Kit' (71 models, CC0) is a platformer-style kit, not a city. Modular Streets Pack: 25 untextured models (2018). Quaternius style differs from Synty and Kenney.

findings.point: Confirmed licence-clean vehicle options exist but police car and van with separate wheels is only partly confirmed.
findings.detail: Kenney Car Kit: sedans, vans, trucks, 8 separate wheels, CC0 (police model unconfirmed on the publisher page). KayKit City Builder Bits: CC0, listing names a Police Car (very small, built for top-down city builders, not first-person detail). Synty City Pack: 8 unique cars x12 variations (police not named). rgsdev 'Free Low Poly Vehicles Pack' (itch/OpenGameArt) says separate wheels and police/taxi; licence per OpenGameArt unverified in this research. For a pursuit mechanic you need an AI-controlled getaway car with visible wheels, so inspect the downloaded GLB for separate wheel nodes before committing.

findings.point: Mixamo animations/characters may be used in commercial games, but raw files may not be distributed, which a web build arguably does.
findings.detail: Adobe community FAQ (posted 2022-09-29, reply 2026-11-08 says 'no rules are changed'): allowed in video games, films, illustrations, merch; prohibited: engine blueprints/templates/asset packages that redistribute raw character or animation files, and any free distribution of raw files; attribution not required; content can't be used to train ML models. Adobe's help page says royalty-free commercial use including games. It requires an Adobe ID login and (from general knowledge, not verified here) exports FBX not GLB, so you convert in Blender. Web build packs the animations into the game, which is normal embedding, but the files are extractable, so there is mild risk. Combined with Quaternius CC0 animations, Mixamo is a gap-filler, not the foundation.

findings.area: Props gap: weapons, camcorder, tape, evidence
findings.point: Props are the weakest category: pistols exist under CC0, but camcorder, police tape, evidence markers and cash bags were not found as licence-clean low-poly models.
findings.detail: Pistols: Quaternius 'Low Poly Guns Pack' (CC0, OpenGameArt, format unconfirmed) and a CC0 derringer with GLB (1,904 tris, 1024px PBR) on OpenGameArt. Cash/masks: Synty Heist (money stacks, 25 masks). Camcorder: searches returned only paid CGTrader/Sketchfab models with unverified licences; the first-person view uses the viewfinder UI, so a simple body can be built in Blender or generated with an AI tool and paid tier. Police tape, cones, barriers: cones and barriers appear in Kenney/Synty city kits as typical contents but I did not verify; tape is trivially made as a textured plane in Godot. Evidence markers are simple geometry (a tent shape with a number) that you or the agent can make in Blender in minutes.

findings.point: Meshy free tier is CC BY 4.0 (attribution required); Pro $20/mo or higher gives private commercial licence; game-ready quality still needs cleanup.
findings.detail: Meshy pricing page: Free $0, 100 credits/mo, 10 assets, CC BY 4.0 with attribution; Pro $20 (1,000 credits), Premium $40 (3,000), Ultra $100 (8,000). Meshy help says paid subscribers can sell without attribution and models generated after a downgrade fall back to CC BY 4.0. Docs say free users 'own' output but under CC BY, a wording inconsistency with the FAQ. Export: FBX, OBJ, USDZ, GLB, STL, Blend, 3MF. Auto-rigging and animation library included (20 on free, 500+ on paid); rigging costs 0 credits per docs. Meshy 7 appeared 2026-08-12; low-poly mode and polycount control are described mainly by resellers, not Meshy docs. Independent reviews say AI meshes need cleanup and UV problems are common; none were tested here. Avoid uploading Synty models to Meshy (Synty EULA forbids uploading to 3D-generation services).

findings.point: Tripo free plan is non-commercial CC BY 4.0; commercial use needs the $20/mo Pro plan.
findings.detail: Per Costbench (third-party, dates inconsistent: verified 2026-10-20 / November 2026): Free = 200 credits/mo (about 13 models), 15 downloads, 10 stored models, non-commercial, CC BY 4.0, public models. Pro $20/mo (yearly billing $240 upfront, 3,000 credits) adds commercial use and private models; Max $90/mo. 3D AI Studio (a competitor, so biased) calls Tripo the 'cleanest game topology', other guides say Tripo meshes are denser and less organised. Tripo's own pricing and licence blog pages returned HTTP 403, so primary terms were not read. Ownership wording unverified.

findings.point: Rodin's licence is per purchase and plan; Hunyuan3D's open licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea.
findings.detail: Hyper3D (Rodin): copyright-license page says purchased content may be sold, redistributed, modified, published; purchase is 'a license, not a transfer of title'; no attribution; cannot be used to train competing AI; no non-infringement warranty. Creator $30/mo (30 credits), Business $120/mo for API (3daistudio, 2026-11-01); Gen-2 supports quad and triangle meshes, GLB/FBX/OBJ/USDZ/STL, 4,000 quad faces on the extra-low preset (runware docs). Hunyuan3D 2.x licence (Hugging Face LICENSE, Section 1.l): Territory = worldwide excluding EU, UK and South Korea; use outside it is unlicensed; licence needed above 1M monthly active users; Tencent claims no rights in outputs; cannot use outputs to improve other AI models. A public web game is playable in the EU/UK, so the creator's own use might be fine but this is risky and unclear; avoid Hunyuan for a public build. Microsoft TRELLIS.2 is MIT-licensed per third-party sources but needs an NVIDIA GPU (24GB+ recommended) and depends on NVIDIA-licensed libraries, so it will not run on the M4 Mac.

findings.point: AI-generated models may not be copyrightable in the US, so you may own little beyond the contract right to use them.
findings.detail: US Copyright Office Part 2 report (2025-01-29): material generated by AI without sufficient human authorship is not eligible for copyright; prompts alone are not enough; human modifications or selection may be protected. Not specific to 3D assets. Practical effect for a free game: you can ship the models under the vendor licence, but you cannot stop others copying them from the web build. Same applies to any asset extractable from a .pck, whatever the source.

findings.point: Safe sources are Freesound filtered to CC0, Sonniss GDC bundles, Kenney audio and Pixabay; avoid NC and CC BY-SA.
findings.detail: Freesound: only CC0 needs no credit; CC BY needs credit; NonCommercial must be avoided; Sampling+ is disputed and being retired (forum threads, user opinions). Sonniss GameAudioGDC bundles: royalty-free, worldwide, no attribution, but you may not resell or redistribute the sounds standalone and may not train AI; the licence text varies by year, and I read only a third-party mirror of the 2023 EULA. Pixabay sound effects: free for commercial use without attribution, but 'standalone' redistribution is restricted (terms page dated 2024-11-18). Kenney audio has 10 packs (Impact, Interface, Sci-fi Sounds, Voiceover Pack, etc.); licence not shown on listing page (his other assets are CC0). No CC0 police-scanner chatter pack was found on Freesound or OpenGameArt; the closest OpenGameArt 'Radio Soldier' voice pack is CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike) and military. Siren, rain and car sounds are plentiful on Freesound CC0 but need per-file checking; I did not verify any specific file.

findings.point: Cleanest options for scanner voices: record yourself and apply a radio filter, or use Kokoro (Apache 2.0); Piper needs per-voice checks; ElevenLabs free is non-commercial.
findings.detail: Kokoro-82M (Hugging Face): Apache-licensed weights, trained on permissive/non-copyrighted audio, 54 voices in 8 languages in v1.0 (Jan 2025); two CC BY datasets are named in training sources (SIWIS CC BY 4.0, Koniwa CC BY 3.0), so keep a credits line to be safe. Piper: engine GPL-3.0-or-later; the project grants no licence over voices; each voice's MODEL_CARD must be traced through its training chain; voices derived from Lessac are research-only; commercially safe voices are listed in COMMERCIAL_USE.md; whether generated audio inherits dataset terms is explicitly 'unsettled' per Piper. Ship the MODEL_CARD. ElevenLabs help centre: free plan has no commercial licence and requires 'elevenlabs.io' credit; all paid plans include a commercial licence. Recording the voices yourself (or friends) with a bandpass + distortion + squelch filter in Godot or Audacity has zero licence risk, and also fits the aesthetic. Apple macOS 'say' voices were not researched and should not be assumed safe.
findings.source_date: Fetched 2026-11-17; Piper docs undated (mention late-2026 retraining)

findings.point: For a camcorder/VCR look, Super-VCR Mono (CC BY 4.0) is the only VCR-style font with a stated licence; Press Start 2P and VT323 are OFL.
findings.detail: Super-VCR Mono by ASmolBoy on DaFont: CC BY 4.0, bitmap font, 181 glyphs, recommended 12px or multiples, no antialiasing; requires credit. VCR OSD Mono and its clones circulate widely, but I found no verified licence for them, and aggregator sites warn about unclear terms; skip. VT323 (SIL OFL 1.1) is a free-commercial terminal font and Press Start 2P is SIL OFL; both permit embedding in games; OFL forbids selling the font alone and requires renamed derivatives. Godot web export embeds the font in the .pck, which OFL allows. Licence notes taken from font-listing sites, not the fonts' official licence files.

findings.point: No licence-clean low-poly police officer or masked-robber set was confirmed; plan to kitbash them.
findings.detail: Quaternius Ultimate Modular Women pack: 10 characters in 4 swappable parts, 24 animations, humanoid rig, CC0, FBX/OBJ/Blend (glTF mentioned), free download; no police outfits mentioned. Kenney Blocky Characters: CC0, 20 files, animations listed; style is blocky (not matching a stylised-realistic cyberpunk look). Synty City Pack: 9 characters; Heist: masks; Sci-Fi Cyber City: 'Street Male', mercenaries. Practical approach: one Synty or Quaternius body, recolour with a police-uniform texture, add Synty masks; this has to be done in Blender. Mixamo has uniformed characters (not verified here).

findings.point: Cheap cyberpunk modular kits exist on Cubebrush/Superhive/itch, but licences and GLB availability need checking.
findings.detail: 3DT Stylized Cyberpunk Downtown Modular Kitbash (Cubebrush/Superhive): 119 pieces, GLB/FBX/.blend, commercial-use claim on a related listing, price not captured; strongest match on look and formats. itch.io 'Cyber City' by papptimus (low-poly modular, pixel-art textures) and DEEZL 'Cyberpunk' (neon billboards, streets): format and licence not stated. Marketplace 'royalty-free' licences (CGTrader, Cubebrush) often forbid redistribution of the raw model, which a web build effectively does, so read the licence for each. Also a Fab convenience-store kit (160 models, 90 products, GLB, 10x14 m store) and an itch 'Convenience Store' PS1-style pack from $4.99; licences were not visible. All differ in style from Synty.

recommendations: Build on Synty POLYGON City Pack ($9.99-$19.99) plus Sci-Fi City ($25-$49.99) as the one consistent family, and add cyberpunk mood in Godot (dark palette, emissive neon, wet roads via roughness/specular, rain particles, glow). Before paying, email Synty support asking in writing whether shipping assets inside a free Godot web build (.pck downloadable by players) is allowed under the One Time Purchase EULA.

Use Kenney CC0 kits (City Kit Roads, Car Kit) as a zero-risk fallback and for prototyping, but avoid mixing them with Synty in final scenes unless you retexture to a shared palette; mixed styles will look inconsistent.

Use Quaternius CC0 Universal Animation Library (Standard free, Source $14.99) and Universal Base Characters for walking/crouch/aim/fall, then check the actual clip names in the download before committing; keep Mixamo as a gap-filler only, with its raw-file redistribution rule in mind.
Do not pay for Synty Sci-Fi Cyber City ($199.99) for a free game: no Godot project, and vehicles are not sedans or police cars.

If using AI 3D: pay for one month of Meshy Pro ($20) or Tripo Pro ($20), generate the missing pieces in one batch (police car, mask variants, camcorder, convenience-store shelves/fridge, evidence markers), then export the GLBs and cancel. Keep screenshots of the licence page and your plan status at generation date. Do not use Hunyuan3D (EU/UK/South Korea excluded) and do not upload Synty models to any generator (EULA forbids it).

Scanner voices: record voice lines yourself (or with friends) and process with a radio filter in Godot; if you want synthetic voices, use Kokoro (Apache 2.0) offline and credit the two CC BY training datasets in a credits file. Avoid ElevenLabs free tier and any Piper voice without a traced MODEL_CARD.
Use only Freesound CC0 (filter by licence) plus Sonniss/Pixabay for ambience, sirens and cars; keep a spreadsheet of every file URL, author and licence from day one.
Use Super-VCR Mono (CC BY 4.0, credit in the in-game credits screen) or VT323 (OFL) for the camcorder overlay; build the REC dot, tape counter and battery as Godot UI.
Create an ASSETS.md ledger (name, URL, price, licence, date downloaded, licence screenshot) and require the coding agent to update it, so a later takedown or audit is easy.
risks: Synty web-build ambiguity: the EULA bans sharing source files outside your team and is silent on web games; a downloadable .pck may be read as distribution. Synty store pages also showed 'Sold out' markers and 429 errors, so prices and availability are unconfirmed.
Synty only officially supports Unity and Unreal per its FAQ; Godot projects are recent (4.5.1 and 4.6.2 listed) and may need work on materials/shaders with Godot 4.7.

Police car, police/robber characters, convenience-store interior, evidence markers, police tape and camcorder were not confirmed in any licence-clean low-poly pack; expect custom Blender work or AI generation.

AI free tiers (Meshy CC BY 4.0, Tripo non-commercial) are traps: models made on free plans can force attribution or ban commercial release, and downgrading later makes new generations fall back to CC BY. Tripo and Rodin terms were not read from primary sources.

Many source pages gave no file formats, counts or per-clip animation lists (Kenney, Quaternius); formats came from itch.io listings and search snippets and must be verified in the downloaded zips (GLB vs glTF vs FBX).
Attribution obligations: Meshy free, Super-VCR Mono, CC BY Freesound files, Kokoro training datasets, and some Piper voices require credit. A credits screen must be in the web build.

Mixamo's rule against distributing raw files and Pixabay/Sonniss standalone-redistribution bans are risks if the web build's .pck is treated as redistributing the raw files; low in practice, but unverified by a lawyer.
AI output is probably not copyrightable in the US, so you cannot stop others from lifting AI-made models from your web build.

Mixed art styles (Synty, Kenney, Quaternius, AI) will clash visually; budget time to unify palettes/textures and polycounts, and note Quaternius base characters average about 13k tris, far above Kenney or Synty props.

verification.topic: Verification of the asset shopping list and licences for a free public web build of a stylized low-poly cyberpunk night-city game (Godot 4.7). Checked 2026-11-17.

verdicts.point: Prices, formats and contents of Synty POLYGON City Pack and Sci-Fi City
verdicts.correction: Prices, formats, asset counts and the 'Sold out' marker all check out. City Pack: $19.99 list / $9.99 sale; Godot 4.5.1 project, Unreal 5.3, Unity 2022.3 and FBX; 331 assets. Sci-Fi City: $49.99 list / $25.00 sale; Godot 4.6.2 project plus FBX; 509 assets. Both pages also show an 'Add to cart' button next to 'Sold out', so availability is unclear rather than unavailable. City Pack characters ship with no animations (Mecanim setup only).

verdicts.point: No confirmed police car or police officer in a licence-clean low-poly set; police are not named in the Synty City Pack
verdicts.correction: The City Pack product page names a Police Car among its 8 cars (with Ambulance, Taxi, Sedan, Van, Muscle Car and others). It also names Male and Female Police Officers among its 9 characters. Sci-Fi City lists a Police Car and a 'Cop 01' character among 20 characters. That closes the police car and police officer gap inside one art family that has Godot projects.

verdicts.point: Synty FAQ says only Unity and Unreal are officially supported
verdicts.correction: Per a search summary of the Synty FAQ (the page itself was not opened): Godot is 'technically possible' but has no official support. This sits awkwardly next to store pages that ship Godot projects. Nothing confirms those projects render correctly on Godot's Compatibility renderer, which a web export uses.

verdicts.point: Synty One Time Purchase licence: in-game use allowed, source files stay inside the team, no uploads to 3D-generation services, 5 seats, silent on web builds
verdicts.correction: All of these points are confirmed on the licence page, which is dated 'As at 9 July 2026'. The report missed one restriction: the licence also bars use in 'Metaverse-related and/or Game Creation Software and products'. A plain web game is probably fine, but any level-editor or modding feature could fall into this. Attribution is not mentioned anywhere on the page. EULA changes do not affect licences already bought.

verdicts.point: Heist, Shops and Shop Interiors packs: contents and Godot support
verdicts.correction: The Synty store returned HTTP 429 for the Heist page during this check, so it was not verified.

verdicts.point: Kenney Car Kit is v2.0 (May 2024) with 40+ models; police model unconfirmed
verdicts.correction: The CC0 licence is confirmed, but the version is out of date. Kenney's page shows v3.1 (3.0 added kart racers), 45 files and a first release in 2022. The page lists no file formats and no model names, so a police car is still unconfirmed at the source.

verdicts.point: Quaternius UAL2: CC0, 130+ animations, free Standard tier and paid Source tier with Godot
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: CC0, 130+ animations, Standard about 60-70% free in OBJ/FBX/glTF, Source adds .blend files and Godot/Unity/Unreal projects. The page shows Patreon claim credits (Silver $10/mo = 15 credits, Gold $20 = 30, Diamond $50 = 75) but states no dollar price for Source in text, so the '$14.99' figure is unverified here. The page lists no clip names. Its listed categories are combos, parkour, farming, fishing and zombie locomotion, so idle, crouch, aim, hands-up and driving clips are unconfirmed.

verdicts.point: Meshy free tier is CC BY 4.0; paid plans are private with commercial use; rigging costs 0 credits
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: free is 100 credits/mo under CC BY 4.0, with commercial use allowed with attribution; all paid plans get a private licence; Remesh and Rigging cost 0 credits. Image-to-3D costs 20 credits on Meshy 7.1 or 6, so the free tier gives roughly 5 models a month. The docs page shows no dollar prices and no downgrade rule, so the $20/$40/$100 prices and the downgrade fallback were not verified here. Because a free game can comply with CC BY, a paid plan is not strictly required; it only removes the attribution duty.

verdicts.point: Tripo free plan is non-commercial CC BY 4.0
verdicts.correction: Tripo's own materials contradict each other. One Tripo blog post says free-tier output is CC BY 4.0 and usable commercially with attribution. A Tripo game-development page says free-plan models do not support commercial use. Read the primary Terms of Service before relying on either claim.

verdicts.point: Hunyuan3D 2 licence: territory excludes EU, UK and South Korea; 1M MAU; no rights claimed in outputs
verdicts.correction: Exact quotes confirmed: Section 1.l (Territory), Section 4 (>1M monthly active users needs Tencent permission), Section 6.d (no claim on Outputs), Section 5.b (outputs may not be used to improve other AI models).

verdicts.point: Kokoro-82M: Apache 2.0, 54 voices in 8 languages, CC BY training datasets
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: v1.0 was released 2025-01-27. SIWIS (CC BY 4.0, under 11 h) and Koniwa (CC BY 3.0, under 1 h) are named as training data.

verdicts.point: Mixamo, Piper, ElevenLabs, Sonniss, Pixabay, fonts, Cubebrush kits, US Copyright Office claims
verdicts.correction: Not re-checked in this pass because of time. Treat them as the original report's claims only.

important_facts_missed: Police content is already covered inside one Synty family. City Pack has a Police Car and Male and Female Police Officers; Sci-Fi City has a Police Car and 'Cop 01'. Kitbashing police or buying AI models for them is unnecessary if Synty is used.
Synty City Pack characters come with no animations, so an animation source is still required. Quaternius CC0 or Mixamo would need retargeting to the Synty rig, and that work is unverified.
The Synty licence also forbids use in 'Game Creation Software' and Metaverse products. Avoid shipping any user level editor or asset-export feature.

Synty's Godot projects were built for Godot 4.5.1 and 4.6.2. Their materials and shaders are not confirmed to work on Godot's Compatibility renderer, which a Godot web export must use. Test one Synty scene in a Compatibility web export before buying more packs.
The report's Kenney Car Kit data is stale. The current version is 3.1 with 45 files, and the publisher page lists no formats or model names.

Meshy's free-tier CC BY 4.0 allows commercial use with attribution, and a free web game can carry a credits line. A paid month is optional, not required, though the free tier gives only about 5 Image-to-3D generations a month at 20 credits each.
Synty store pages show both 'Sold out' and 'Add to cart' at once, so the marker probably means sale stock or a display glitch rather than a hard sell-out. Still check at purchase time.
Godot's PCK encryption needs custom-compiled export templates. For a web build, assume every asset will be extractable from the .pck.
verification.corrected_bottom_line: Synty POLYGON City Pack ($9.99 sale / $19.99 list, Godot 4.5.1 project) plus Sci-Fi City ($25 sale / $49.99 list, Godot 4.6.2 project) remain the best single family. The report's police gap is wrong: both packs include a Police Car, City Pack has Male and Female Police Officers, and Sci-Fi City has a cop character. The remaining real gaps are animations (City Pack ships none), a convenience-store interior, masked robbers (Heist pack not re-verified), the camcorder, tape and evidence markers. The Synty licence (dated 9 July 2026) allows shipping assets in your products, keeps source files inside your team, forbids AI 3D generation and use in game-creation software, and says nothing on web builds. Asking Synty in writing remains sensible, and the Godot projects should be tested on the Compatibility (web) renderer before buying more. Kenney (Car Kit v3.1, CC0) and Quaternius UAL2 (CC0) are confirmed zero-risk fallbacks; UAL2's clip names and Source price are unverified. Meshy's free CC BY 4.0 tier is usable with attribution for a free game. Tripo's free-tier commercial status is contradictory, even in Tripo's own materials. Hunyuan3D's EU/UK/South Korea exclusion is confirmed, so avoid it.

research.topic: Free hosting for a Godot 4.7 web export (Cloudflare Pages, Workers assets + R2, GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, itch.io)
research.summary: Godot 4.7's web export is single-threaded by default (since 4.3), so no COOP/COEP headers are needed and any static host works. Threads and GDExtensions need those two headers (or the PWA service-worker workaround). The stock release .wasm is probably around 20 MB uncompressed, but I found no official figure. Only community numbers exist (one blog reports a 42 MB total default export; one write-up reports a ~19-20 MB wasm). That is under Cloudflare's confirmed 25 MiB per-file cap, but only just, and the .pck will exceed it once the game has real art and audio. Cloudflare Pages is the best free fit: static requests are reported unlimited and it has _headers support, custom domains and automatic Brotli/gzip. Its one real problem is the 25 MiB file cap, which a large .pck will hit. The workaround is to split the pck or serve it from R2 (free tier 10 GB, zero egress fees, 5 TiB per object). GitHub Pages is the simplest fallback (1 GB site, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, on-the-fly gzip, but no custom headers). itch.io is a good second place to publish: 500 MB extracted, 200 MB per file, automatic gzip for .wasm and .pck, and an experimental SharedArrayBuffer toggle that I could not verify in the official docs. My strongest verified findings are the official limit pages. My weakest are the stock wasm size, Netlify and Vercel per-file limits, and content-policy details for most hosts, because I could not confirm them.

findings.point: Godot 4.7 web export is single-threaded by default, so no COOP/COEP headers are required.
findings.detail: Official 4.7 docs call single-threaded export 'the preferred and now default way' (added in 4.3). Thread Support and Extensions Support are opt-in and require 'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin' and 'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp', plus a secure context. Without them a threaded build does not run. The Progressive Web App > Enable option adds the headers via a service worker. The docs do not state the default value of the Thread Support checkbox for 4.7, only that single-threaded is the preferred export.

findings.point: Web export is Compatibility renderer (WebGL 2.0) only; Safari has extra WebGL 2.0 issues; audio is limited.
findings.detail: Docs say Forward+ and Mobile are unsupported and WebGPU is not supported. Chromium or Firefox are recommended, because Safari has WebGL 2.0 issues. Since 4.3, web audio defaults to Sample playback via Web Audio, with no audio effects, reverb, doppler or procedural audio. The viewfinder, neon and rain look must be built for Compatibility on the web. One secondary source claims a 4.7 wasm64 option, but the official 4.7 web page does not mention it, so treat that claim as unverified.

findings.point: No official size for the stock 4.7 release .wasm; community figures put it near 20 MB uncompressed.
findings.detail: Official docs give no figure, only that gzip shrinks the wasm to 'around a quarter' of its size. A blog post (popcar.bearblog.dev, Godot 4.x, date not confirmed) measured a default web export of 42.0 MB total, 39.1 MB with optimize=size, 31.5 MB without 3D, 17.4 MB with a custom build. Another write-up (jacobfilipp.com, anecdote) says the engine .wasm is about 20 MB and gzip took one index.wasm from 19 MB to 5 MB. The Godot size-history site was fetched but showed no numbers. Not confirmed: the exact 4.7 byte size. The stock web template is not installed locally, so measure it after installing the template.

findings.point: 25 MiB max per file, 20,000 files per site on Free.
findings.detail: Official limits page: 'Max file size 25 MiB' per site asset, 20,000 files on Free (100,000 on paid plans, which requires setting PAGES_WRANGLER_MAJOR_VERSION=4). Builds: 500 per month on Free, 20 min timeout. Custom domains: 100 per project on Free. Projects: 100 per account. The page suggests R2 for larger files. The 25 MiB figure is confirmed as current. The page does not list a total site size limit or a bandwidth limit.

findings.point: Static requests are reported unlimited and free. Brotli/gzip is automatic. A _headers file works for COOP/COEP.
findings.detail: The serving-pages docs say Pages serves Gzip and Brotli 'whenever possible', sets Content-Type per file and adds nosniff. Wasm is not specifically mentioned. A _headers file allows 100 rules with up to 2,000 characters per header and can add COOP/COEP. A search result summarising Cloudflare's pricing docs says static requests are free and unlimited on Free and paid plans. I did not open that pricing page myself, and the limits page lists no bandwidth cap. Cloudflare's docs recommend not overriding caching with custom Cache Rules. Range requests currently return 200, not 206. Pages sends max-age=0, must-revalidate, so returning players revalidate with an ETag.

findings.point: Same 25 MiB per-file and 20,000-file limits on Workers Free.
findings.detail: Official Workers limits page: 20,000 files per Worker version on Free (100,000 paid, needs Wrangler 4.34.0+), 25 MiB per individual file on both plans. The Free plan's general 100,000 requests/day limit applies to Worker invocations, and the page lists no separate static-assets request limit. Other Cloudflare sources say static asset requests are free. So there is no per-file advantage over Pages, and Pages is the simpler tool for a purely static game.

findings.point: R2 can hold the big .pck: 10 GB free, zero egress fees, up to 5 TiB per object.
findings.detail: R2 pricing: free tier 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B operations per month, no egress fees including r2.dev. Limits page: 5 TiB per object, 5 GiB single-part upload. The r2.dev endpoint is rate-limited, 'meant for testing', so production should use a custom domain on a Cloudflare-managed zone. A separate-origin .pck needs CORS configured on the bucket. The 'Free plan applies only to Standard storage'. I could not confirm how many sources document exactly how a Godot page loads a .pck from another origin. That needs testing, and the HTML shell's fetch of the .pck is the thing to modify.

findings.point: 1 GB site limit, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10 builds/hour soft; Godot docs say it provides on-the-fly gzip.
findings.detail: Official limits page: published sites no larger than 1 GB, 100 GB soft monthly bandwidth, 10 soft builds per hour (not applicable with a custom Actions workflow), deploy timeout 10 minutes. No per-file limit is stated for Pages itself, but the repo blocks files over 100 MiB and warns at 50 MiB, and browser uploads cap at 25 MiB. Git LFS files are the usual trouble. Usage rules: not free hosting for an online business or a site mainly for commercial transactions or commercial SaaS. GitHub's terms ban obscene content and violent or threatening content. The official Godot web docs say GitHub Pages provides on-the-fly gzip. GitHub Pages cannot set custom response headers, so threaded builds would need the PWA service-worker workaround. Custom domains are supported (known, not re-verified in this pass).

findings.point: Credit-based Free plan: 300 credits/month, hard limit; bandwidth costs 20 credits/GB, so roughly 15 GB/month if all credits went to bandwidth.
findings.detail: The Netlify credit-plans page lists no fixed bandwidth allowance and no file size limit for Free. Bandwidth is 20 credits per GB, web requests 2 credits per 10,000, each production deploy 15 credits, 300 credits/month, hard limit with no auto recharge, so the site stops at the limit. That page has no date stamp. Free-plan behaviour at 0 credits is not specified on the page, and I could not confirm the per-file limit. This is far tighter than the older '100 GB/month' figure many tutorials quote. Custom headers are supported via a _headers file or [[headers]] in netlify.toml, so COOP/COEP are possible. I did not verify Brotli/gzip handling or custom domains in this pass.
findings.source_date: undated docs page; check before relying

findings.point: 100 GB Fast Data Transfer/month and 100 MB static upload via CLI; the Hobby plan has long been personal/non-commercial, but I did not confirm that wording in the pages I read.
findings.detail: Hobby plan page (updated 2026-11-12) lists First 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 1,000,000 CDN requests, 100 deployments/day, 50 domains per project. The limits page (2026-09-16) says Static File uploads are 100 MB on Hobby (1 GB Pro), applied to the source files uploaded via CLI. No per-file limit was stated. Over-limit on Hobby means waiting 30 days. Custom headers via vercel.json or config can set COOP/COEP (known, not verified in this pass). The page excerpt did not show the fair-use 'never fair use' list. Not confirmed: a Hobby non-commercial restriction. For a free public game this matters only if ads or sales are added.

findings.point: HTML5 zip: max 1,000 files, 500 MB extracted, 200 MB per file, 240-character path.
findings.detail: Official HTML5 docs: those exact limits. The CDN automatically gzips uncompressed files with extensions including html, js, css, svg, wasm, wav, glb and pck. Files ending in .br are served as Brotli. Embed in page needs fixed dimensions, or Click to launch in fullscreen. The page does not mention SharedArrayBuffer or COOP/COEP, so I could not confirm it from official docs. Search results show itch has an experimental 'SharedArrayBuffer support' checkbox under embed options (forum posts, anecdote) with reports of Firefox issues. Godot's own docs recommend single-threaded export as more compatible with itch.io, Poki and CrazyGames. An itch.io page lives under itch.io's domain, not your own custom domain. Their custom-domain feature is a paid-style option I did not verify.

findings.point: Crime scenes and some blood are likely fine on all six, but only itch.io and GitHub's rules were actually read.
findings.detail: itch.io's quality guidelines have no dedicated violence or gore section. Projects with strong adult themes must be marked via Metadata > Classification, adult pages are hidden from users without the setting on, and shock-value-only premises can be delisted. GitHub's page cites its Terms: no obscene content and no violent or threatening content, which is vague; 'some blood' in a stylised game is very probably OK but it is a discretionary rule. Cloudflare's website terms page I fetched says it does not apply to self-serve products and the Pages terms were not retrieved. I did not open Netlify or Vercel acceptable-use policies. The correct statement is 'not confirmed'.

findings.point: Pre-compression and size reduction are documented; a custom export template can shrink the wasm.
findings.detail: Godot docs: serve .wasm as application/wasm and .pck as application/octet-stream, compress both, and build an optimized export template with unused features disabled. The blog source says optimize=size, no 3D and removing Vulkan (irrelevant on Compatibility) cut a default 42 MB export to 17-31 MB. This game is 3D, so the 'no 3D' saving is not available and the build must keep it. Building a custom template means compiling Godot with SCons and Emscripten, which is an AI-agent task but adds toolchain work. GitHub Pages and itch.io need no pre-compression because they gzip on the fly.

findings.point: One community claim says Cloudflare's terms limit serving large non-HTML content disproportionately; unconfirmed from official text.
findings.detail: A community-forum answer (anecdote, undated, and the pricing docs referenced were updated about 71 days before the search) says there is no bandwidth cap provided you follow the terms. I looked for the self-serve terms but the page I fetched excluded them, so I could not verify whether a very heavy game download falls under any 'disproportionate non-HTML' clause. That clause existed historically for the CDN service; for Pages and R2 it is not confirmed here.

recommendations: Primary hosting: Cloudflare Pages (free), with a _headers file ready for Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy/Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy in case threads are ever turned on. The creator has no Cloudflare account yet, so account creation is a step for them.
Ship the single-threaded web export first (the 4.7 default) so no special headers are needed, and treat threads as an optional later experiment.

Measure the real stock web template .wasm and the game .pck as soon as the web template is installed. If any single file is over 25 MiB (a .pck almost certainly will be), either split content into multiple .pck files each under 25 MiB, or serve the .pck from R2 behind a custom domain with CORS set. Test this early with a dummy big file.

Plan the asset budget now: keep textures, audio and models compact (compressed formats, short loops, no raw video), because download size drives the free-tier bandwidth and the player's first-load wait.
Keep a second build target on itch.io (zip under 500 MB extracted and 200 MB per file) as a discovery channel and a backup; use the single-threaded export so no SharedArrayBuffer setting is needed.

Fallback hosting: GitHub Pages if the game fits under 1 GB and no file hits the 100 MiB repository block (use a Pages deploy via Actions rather than committing the build). It gzips on the fly, but cannot set headers.

Do not rely on Netlify Free for a large game: the credit system makes bandwidth about 20 credits per GB against a 300-credit hard limit. Vercel Hobby (100 GB/month) is workable but confirm per-file limits and commercial-use terms first.

Before launch, read the Cloudflare Pages and R2 terms of service directly, and the GitHub and itch.io content rules, then tag the game appropriately (itch adult/violence classification) for the crime scenes and blood.
risks: The stock 4.7 wasm size is unconfirmed; if it is above 25 MiB (the unflattering case), Cloudflare Pages cannot host it directly without a custom size-optimized template or splitting, which a wasm cannot do. The reported ~20 MB figure leaves little margin.

A .pck for a 3D game with textures and audio will very likely exceed 25 MiB, forcing the pck-splitting or R2 workaround. Custom loading from another origin involves editing the generated HTML shell and CORS, which has not been tested.

Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare limits and pricing change frequently; the Netlify page was undated and the Cloudflare 'unlimited static requests' claim came from a search summary rather than a page I opened.
Threaded builds need COOP/COEP; GitHub Pages cannot set headers and itch's SharedArrayBuffer toggle is experimental with reported Firefox problems, so threads are risky on those hosts.
Safari has WebGL 2.0 issues per the Godot docs and the Compatibility renderer is the only web option, so the full shaded cyberpunk look must be tested on Chrome, Firefox and Safari.

R2's r2.dev endpoint is rate-limited and for testing only; production use needs a custom domain, which means owning a domain on a Cloudflare zone.
